VERS. 19.-- *Euntes.* Qui jam in lucem venit, quod hactenus quibusdam de causis dubium hominibus fuerat. *Docete.* Congruus ordo. Primo enim docendus est auditor. Deinde fidei sacramentis imbuendus, tunc ad servanda mandata instruendus. Quia nisi prius anima fidem recipiat, non est dandus baptismus, nec valet mundari, si post non insistat bonis operibus.

VERS. 20.-- *Et ecce ego vobiscum sum.* Quae autem [0178D] merces piae conversationis, quodve pignus futurae beatitudinis etiam in praesenti sit fidelibus, subdit: *Ecce ego vobiscum sum,* etc. Quod apostolis per successiones universali Ecclesiae promittit. Nota quod usque in finem saeculi non sunt desituri qui divina mansione sunt digni.

[n: (AUG.)] Prima sabbati diluculo, etc., *usque ad* dicente eis angelo: *Sic veniet quemadmodum vidistis eum euntem in coelum [n: (Act. I)]*.
english:
## PROLOGUE.

[0063A]

Matthew, when he had first preached the Gospel in Judaea, wishing to pass over to the Gentiles, was the first to write the Gospel in Hebrew: which he left for a remembrance to the brethren from whom he was going. For as it was necessary that the Gospel be preached for the confirmation of the faith, so also that it be written against the heretics. But although many have written a Gospel, only four have the [0063B] testimony of authority: because through the four quarters of the world they announce the faith of the Trinity, and they are as it were four wheels in the Lord's chariot, which bears him through the preaching of the Gospel, and the human race, destroyed by a fourfold [0064A] death, was to be quickened by their preaching: whence also the gospels of the others fell away, nor were they received: because they were unwilling that the predetermined number should be brought to an end, on account of the power of the sacrament. The evangelists are also designated by four figures, which are not deceptive, but conscious to themselves of a delightful mystery. Matthew is understood in the man: because he dwells principally upon the humanity of Christ. Mark in the [0064B] lion, because he treats of the resurrection. Luke in the calf, treating of the priesthood. John in the eagle, writing the sacraments of the Divinity. But Christ, whom they describe, was a man born of a virgin: a calf in the immolation, [0065A] a lion in the resurrection, an eagle in the ascension. Or in the man is expressed humanity, in the calf priesthood, in the lion kingship, in the eagle the sacrament of the Divinity.

*Here begins the Gospel according to Matthew.*



## CHAPTER ONE.

VERS. 1.-- *The book of the generation. [n: (HIER.)]* The Hebrews impose upon their volumes a name taken from their beginnings, as the book of Genesis, etc., *as far as* but this custom holds in many, chiefly in the prophets, as "the vision of Isaiah," where thou suppliest, "this is."

*Of the son of David.* The order is inverted, lest, Abraham being set first, the connected sequence of the generation should be broken. Of these [0065B] two he is specially called Son: because the one was first among the patriarchs, the other among the kings, to whom the promise concerning Christ was made, that he might disclose to the Jews that Christ was to come out of the law, in whom they should see the prophecies fulfilled.

*Of the son of David the son of Abraham.* He chose these two out of all, whose Son Christ is called, that to the Jews to whom he writes, who knew from the law that Christ was to come, it might appear that this is he who had long been promised, in whom all the prophecies should be seen to be fulfilled; for to these alone in the Old Testament is the promise of Abraham recorded as made, *and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed [n: (Gen. XXII)]*.

Abraham and David are two pillars standing in the law as in a porch before the door which is Christ: [0065C] which a cord of twelve cubits encircles, that is, the faith of the apostles. He embraces these fathers in the genealogy, from the midst of whom Christ the door is opened to believers.

VERS. 2.-- *Abraham begot Isaac: and Isaac begot Jacob.* Fittingly let the beginning of the generation be from him to whom he was first promised, in whom is the blessing of all.

Matthew begins the generation from the beginning of the promise. And even to the end of the book this is pursued, that he who was born of this generation may be understood as God and man.

From the outset he begins from him to whom the promise of faith was first made, that in this father, to whom the promise was first made, they may learn who and what manner of men they ought to be who [0065D] wish to be blessed in his seed. Matthew begins, or reckons, the generation by descending: because he shows the humanity of Christ, through which God descended to men. Luke, relating it by ascending, discloses the form of the sacrament. For beginning from the baptism he ascends as far as God, showing that the baptized ascend to this, that they may be sons of God.

*Begot.* Matthew sets down, *begot:* he who numbers only the sons of nature. Luke: *Who was:* he who inserts some who are sons according to the law or by adoption. Matthew sets down "genuit," and not "generavit," perhaps that he might be recognized, shown forth at the end, of whom it is said: *This day have I begotten thee [n: (Psal. II)]*.

*Judas and his brethren.* Therefore Judas alone is named expressly, [0066A] that thou mightest recognize him who had been promised out of his stock.

He mentions the brethren of Judas, the brethren of Isaac and Jacob being passed over: because those were driven off from the people of God as strangers: these were written as heirs in the book of life, and are as it were the twelve patriarchs, in whom the number of the apostles also is signified. But they are not expressed by name, lest the generation be extended beyond the number of the sacrament.

In the seed of the aforesaid fathers Christ entered into Egypt, and the enemy, foreboding this, oppressed the people, and slew not the women, but the males, that he might extinguish him.

From Judas is Christ, whom all the Gentiles received: at whose coming Herod, a foreigner, was already ruling.

[0066B]VERS. 3.-- *And Judas.* Judas begot Phares and Zaram before he entered Egypt, into which both afterwards passed over with their father.

*And Phares begot Esrom.* In Egypt Phares begot Esrom, and Esrom Aram, and Aram Aminadab, and Aminadab Naasson: and then Moses led them out of Egypt. Naasson was leader under Moses in the tribe of Judah through the desert, in which he begot Salmon. This Salmon was prince in the tribe of Judah, who entered with Joshua into the land of promise. This Salmon in the land of promise begot Booz of Raab.

Christ is Phares, that is, division, because he will separate the sheep from the goats. He himself is Esrom, that is, an arrow or a court, because he pierces the hearts of his hearers. He has also [0066C] the breadth of charity, wherewith he loved even his enemies.

VERS. 4.-- *And Aram.* Aram is interpreted *Christ the elect* or *the exalted*: the Elect, of whom the prophet says: *Behold my servant whom I have chosen [n: (Ose. XI)]*. And elsewhere: *The Lord is high above all nations [n: (Psal. CXII)]*. He himself is Aminadab, that is, willing, who says: *I will freely sacrifice to thee [n: (Ibid. XXXIII)]*. The same is Naasson, that is, augury, who knows things past, present and to come. Or Naasson, serpentine, because Christ after the manner of a serpent guarded against all snares.

VERS. 5.-- *And Salmon begot Booz.* Christ is Salmon, that is, *perceiving,* because he perceives all things. He himself took Raab, that is, the Church of the Gentiles. Raab, *hunger,* or *blessedness,* or *onrush:* because the Church of the Gentiles hungers and thirsts after justice, and, spread abroad through [0066D] the world, converts philosophers and kings by the onrush of doctrine. Raab displayed the scarlet in the window, that is, in the mouth she declares the passion of Christ by confession. Raab the harlot, who received the messengers of Joshua, whom Salmon, prince of the tribe of Judah, joined to himself, signifies the Church of the Gentiles, which is joined to the prince out of Judah, that is, to Christ. And she alone with her own is saved, while Jericho, that is, the present world, walled about with seven walls of vices, is beset for the space of seven days with the trumpets of preachings, until *at the last trump* all the walls fall down, and the last death is destroyed.

*And Booz.* Booz is Christ, of whom it is said: *Behold the Lord God shall come with strength [n: (Isa. XL)]*. Note [0067A] that none of the holy women is taken into the genealogy of Christ, but those whom Scripture reproves. For he ought to be born of sinners, who had come for sinners, that his own might learn that the sins of the fathers do not stand in their way. Whence the lamb to be immolated at the Passover was commanded to be taken from the goats and the sheep, that is, to be begotten from the just and from sinners

*Of Ruth.* A Moabitess, that he may show the prophecy of Isaiah fulfilled: *Send forth the lamb, O Lord, the ruler of the earth [n: (Isa. XVI)]*. Through her the seed of Abraham is brought down to Christ. The Church of the Gentiles, signified by Ruth, before she came to Booz, that is, to Christ, was of her father the devil.

Ruth signifies the Church which is of Moab, that is, of the Gentiles, which [was] of her father the devil and of the rock of the desert [0067B] because of idolatry, out of which God raised up sons of Abraham: forgetful of her former nation she came to Booz, who is called strong, that is, to Christ, who raises up the seed of his brother, that is, of Moses, who died without children, *because the law brought nothing to perfection [n: (Hebr. VII)]*. Ruth, *seeing* or *hastening;* because the Church with a pure heart sees God, which hastens to the prize of the heavenly vision and determines to persevere in faith and love.

*And Jesse.* The father of David is more often named Isai, but he bore two names. Yet here he is called Jesse for this reason: that he might know that he had come; of whom Isaiah says: *There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse [n: (Isa. XI)]*, etc. This is the flower which Isaac smells, saying: *Behold the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field [n: (Gen. XXVII)]*, because the Spirit filled him most abundantly.

[0067C] *King.* Not that he alone is king in this genealogy, but because he is the first king of Judah and the beginning of the kings, for whose sake the rest also are kept upon the throne of the kingdom: and through him the order of the generation runs down to Christ, who has the kingdom of David.

VERS. 6.-- *And David the king.* Mystically David, that is, Christ, who overcame Goliath, that is, the devil. He himself is strong of hand, or desirable in aspect. Of the same it is said: *The Lord strong and mighty [n: (Psal. XXIII)]*, etc. And again: *Beautiful in form above the sons of men [n: (Ibid. XLIV)]*.

*Of Urias.* Urias, my light, namely of God, that is, the devil, who said: *I will be like the Most High [n: (Isa. XIV)]*: whose wedded wife, the Church, Christ loved from the upper chamber of the Father's majesty, and, when she was made fair, joined her to himself [0067D] in marriage. Urias, who is a figure of the devil, is interpreted *my light is God*, who still transforms himself into an angel of light, and makes himself the light of God.

VERS. 7.-- *And Solomon.* Christ is Solomon, that is, *peaceable,* because he himself is our peace, who made both one. He himself is Roboam, that is, the onrush of a people, who swiftly converts peoples to the faith. *Roboam.* Of him it is said: *I will give to Roboam himself the tribe of Judah, that a lamp may remain to David all his days in Israel [n: (III Reg. XI)]*. [var: Vulg. 3 Reg. 11:36 reads *filio autem ejus dabo tribum unam, ut remaneat lucerna David servo meo cunctis diebus coram me in Jerusalem*, "to his son I will give one tribe, that a lamp may remain to David my servant all his days before me in Jerusalem"] Which cannot be taken according to the letter, because neither did Israel endure for all days, nor after Christ was there any leader of David's line in Israel. But Christ is an eternal lamp in the heavenly Israel, and therefore is kept always. But Christ is said [0068A] to sit upon the throne of David, because David's temporal kingdom prefigured the eternal kingdom of Christ. *Abias.* The Lord is Father, that is, Christ, who says: *I will be to him a Father, for as Lord he has done all things whatsoever he would [n: (Psal. CXIII)]*. Who is also Asa, that is, lifting up, because he himself took away the sins of the world.

VERS. 8.-- *Josaphat,* etc. *Judging* or *the judgment of God,* namely Christ, who judges the world in equity. *And Joram begot.* Christ is Joram, that is, exalted, who says: *No man ascends into heaven but he who descended from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven [n: (Joan. III)]*.

VERS. 9.-- *And Ozias.* Under Ozias, Joathan, Achaz and Ezechias, Isaiah prophesied concerning Christ. Because of the sins of the princes the mouths of the prophets were shut. [0068B] *Ezechias.* The Lord is strong, he it is who says to the apostles: *Fear not.* To Ezechias, when he was without children, it was said: *Set thy house in order, for thou shalt die and shalt not live [n: (Isa. XXXVIII)]*. Therefore he wept not for the sake of a longer life, since he knew that Solomon had for that very reason pleased God, because he had not asked for more years: but because he was in doubt whether the promise of God would be fulfilled, when he knew himself to be of the stock of David, through whom Christ must needs come: and he himself was without children, whence also he said [n: (Ibid. XXXVIII)]: *I shall not see the Lord God,* likewise, *I shall not look upon man any more,* etc. On the contrary he believed, because he who had promised is faithful. But God changes the sentence which he had given, for the testing of faith, and grants space for begetting.

VERS. 10.-- *Manasses.* Forgetful. This is he who [0068C] said, as it were to a converted sinner: *I will not remember all his iniquities [n: (Ezech. XVIII)]*. *Amon,* that is, *faithful* or *a fosterer,* signifying Christ, of whom it is said: *The Lord is faithful in all his ways, who calls his sons together, as a hen her chicks [n: (Psal. CXLIV)]*. [var: Vulg. Ps. 144:13 reads *Fidelis Dominus in omnibus verbis suis*, "faithful in all his words"; *in omnibus viis suis* belongs to Ps. 144:17, *Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis*, and the clause about the hen stands nowhere in the psalm (cf. Matt. XXIII)]

VERS. 11.-- *Josias,* that is, *the salvation of the Lord* or *incense.* He it is who says: *Let my prayer be directed as incense [n: (Psal. CXL)]*, etc.

Josias, a just king, which his sons whom he begot were not; not in the transmigration, because he never went into transmigration: but according to God's predestination to the transmigration, he sets Jechonias and his brethren together, that of those whose iniquity is common the misery also may be alike. Jechonias, the preparation of the Lord, because the Lord prepared both the father and the son for the transmigration.



## CHAPTER ONE. (cont.)

[0068D] [n: (ISID.)] The truth of the history holds that there were two Jechoniases, so that the one, namely the father, stands at the end of the preceding fourteen, the other at the beginning of the following. But mystically, according to Augustine, one and the same is in the faith of the preceding and at the beginning of the following. But why has Joachim, the father of Jechonias, been passed over? Perhaps, that he might make Jechonias a type of Christ, he numbered him twice, and passed Joachim over lest the number should be increased.

All who are numbered from David to the transmigration of Babylon were kings.

*Jechonias.* The former Jechonias is called *the resurrection of the Lord,* the latter Jechonias *the preparation of the Lord.* Both [0069A] agree with Christ, who is *the resurrection and the life [n: (Joan. XI)]*.

VERS. 12.-- *Salathiel.* My petition is God, it agrees with Christ, who says: *Holy Father, keep them whom thou hast given me, that they may be one as we also are [n: (Joan. XVII)]*.

VERS. 13.-- *And Zorobabel begot Abiud.* The master of Babylon, that is, of confusion. It agrees with him who called the world back from the error of idolatry to the way of truth. There were zealous men from among the Jews called Heriles on account of the nearness of Christ's kindred, and they were Nazaraeans, who, retaining the order of Christ's genealogy partly by memory, partly from the books of Days, partly from grandfathers and great-grandfathers, wrote it down in order. *Abiud,* that is, *my father.* This agrees with Christ, of whom it is said: *He hath called upon me: thou art my father* [0069B] [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII)], etc. [var: Vulg. Ps. 88:27 reads *Ipse invocabit me*, "He shall call upon me": the future, where Migne prints the perfect *invocavit*] *Eliachim.* The Lord raising up. He who says: *Every one who sees the Son and believes in him shall have life everlasting, and I will raise him up [n: (Joan. VI)]*, etc.

VERS. 14.-- *Azor.* Helped. He it is who says: *Behold God hath helped me, the Lord is the upholder of my soul [n: (Psal. LIII)]*. [var: Vulg. Ps. 53:6 reads *Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me*, "Behold, for God helpeth me": the present, where Migne prints the perfect *adjuvit*, answering to his own etymology of the name, "Helped"] *Sadoch.* Just, that is, Christ, of whom it is said: *The Lord is just and hath loved justices [n: (Ibid. X)]*. *Achim,* that is, *this my brother.* Who else than he who willed to be made man, that he might have brethren, of whom he should say: *I will declare thy name to my brethren [n: (Ibid. XXI)]*. *Eliud,* that is, my God, it agrees with Christ, who says: *My God, why hast thou forsaken me [n: (Matth. XXVII)]*?

VERS. 15.-- *Eleazar,* that is, *my God is my helper.* [0069C] He it is who said in the person of man: *My God, I will hope in him [n: (Psal. XC)]*. *Mathan.* Giving or given. He it is who gave good things to men, and of whom it is said: *So God loved the world, that he gave his Son [n: (Joan. III)]*.

Through these fathers Christ [came] into the world, and bore in himself the office of them all. And it is fitting that we ascend to him by that same line of holiness by which he deigned to descend to us.

VERS. 16.-- *Joseph.* One who adds. Christ, who added the Gentiles to the Jews, who is also called the father of Christ, whom, born of his own wife, he received by adoption: but he is also called father by supposition. *Joseph* Matthew calls the son of Jacob, and Jacob the son of Mathan. Luke calls Joseph the son of Heli, and Heli the son of Mathat; but Mathan and [0069D] Mathat begot one son each of the same wife, Hesta by name. Mathan, who descended through Solomon, married her first, and, leaving one son, Jacob, died, and afterwards Mathat, who descended from David through Mathan, married the same woman and begot Heli, thus Jacob and Heli are brothers by the same mother. But Jacob, taking the wife of Heli his brother, who had died without children, to raise up his seed, begot Joseph, his own by nature, but by the law the son of Heli. That the son is said to be called by the name of him for whom he is raised up, is not true, since Booz called him whom he begot of Ruth not Elimelech, for whom he was raised up, but Obeth.

*The husband of Mary.* What has the generation traced from David down to Joseph to do with Christ, since Christ is not of the seed [0070A] of Joseph? But it is not the custom of the Scriptures that the order of women should be woven into the generations; and therefore it is brought in not through Mary, but through Joseph, since Joseph and Mary were of one tribe. Whence also he was compelled to take her as a kinswoman, lest one tribe should be confounded with another: whence also they make their declaration together, as of one stock, returning to Bethlehem when each went to his own city.

By the example of Mary it is clear to faithful married persons that, an equal consent being kept, continence can abide, and that it is called a marriage not by the mingling of bodily sex, but by the guarding of the mind's affection. Whence also Joseph is called the husband of Mary, because a marriage is true where the effect of love is preserved, and in Mary the fruit of the nuptials is found.

[0070B]VERS. 17.-- *All therefore.* The order of the generation having at length been run through, the evangelist, concluding at the end, recapitulates under a mystical number.

VERS. 18.-- *Now the generation of Christ.* He sets it down without the addition, "Jesu," that thou mayest understand him of whom the prophet says: *Thy God hath anointed thee.* The name Jesus, which belongs to him substantially, he reserves for the angel, so that he who is afterwards to speak of the conception of the Holy Spirit may the more sublimely set forth his proper name from the office of salvation. *So it was.* As has been said, that from Joseph the origin of Mary, who was also of David, might be made clear: and Christ, not of his seed, is shown as God and man, as man through the genealogy, as God through this, that he was of a virgin by the Holy Spirit. So, I say, it was, as has been written above and will presently be said, as afterwards it is made manifest by signs and prodigies, [0070C] so that the whole book may demonstrate that God and man was born: which must be believed that it may be understood. For here human sense fails, where there is not nature, but power: he who does not believe does not understand that a virgin brought forth, that the word was made flesh.

*When she had been espoused. [n: (ORIG.)]* She was espoused for this reason, that she might signify the Church, which is virgin and spouse: and that through Joseph, etc., *as far as* the espousal was made some days before the constant cohabitation, and in the meantime she was a wife under the guardianship of her husband.

*Before they came together.* Not that they came together afterwards: as if we should say, before he repented, he was overtaken by death. Not that they came together afterwards; but he shows the time next to the nuptials, in which the solemnities of the nuptials are celebrated.

[0070D] *She was found with child.* Joseph found that she was with child, but did not know that it was of the Holy Spirit: since afterwards, as one in doubt, he deliberated to put her away; but the apostle adds this, lest in the meantime a suspicion should creep upon the reader. How this was done, and in what order, or in what city the conception of Christ was accomplished, this, being here passed over, is set forth by Luke.

VERS. 19.-- *Just.* By the faith whereby he believed that Christ was to be born of a virgin, and he willed to humble himself before so great a grace.

That he was just, this is a testimony to the chastity of Mary, so that he who preserves the innocent may be called just: but merciful also in that he was unwilling to make it public, just from his knowledge of her chastity, merciful from fear. He knew that she was [0071A] blameless: but whence or what the matter was he did not know: and therefore he chose a middle way of escape, that he might neither betray the innocent, nor by consenting to a thing unknown make himself guilty before God. It is true virtue when there is neither mercy without justice, nor justice without mercy, which, separated from one another, fall away.

*And would not have her.* Whom he had espoused, to lead into marriage, lest he should seem to conceal what he did not know. Or to expose her to a punishment in which he knew there was no infamy, because he knew that he had received her a virgin and had kept her untouched.

VERS. 20.-- *But while he thought on these things.* Here we are taught that in uncertain matters we must deliberate long, lest we sin by the rashness of levity. *Behold the angel of the Lord.* Because he thinks thus mercifully, he deserves to be consoled, and his own counsel [0071B] is changed for a better counsel. *Son of David.* Acknowledge what was promised to the house of David, of which thou art, and Mary also, and see it fulfilled in her. *Fear not.* Although it be as great as thou believest, yet fear not on account of guilt, but embrace her with the regard of charity. *Thy wife.* She was a wife not by intercourse, but by affection, not by the joining of bodies, but by the coupling of souls.

Note that she is called wife from the first pledge of the espousal. It is therefore a matter of dispensation if any one is permitted to marry another after the sacrament of betrothal, and if he can never pay the debt.

Rightly is Joseph called husband, and Mary wife, since in him the affection of love is preserved, which is true marriage, and in her without intercourse there is the fruit of the nuptials.

*It is born in her.* To be born of her is to be brought forth into the light. [0071C] But to be born in her is to be conceived; or according to the presence of the angel which he has from God: to whom the future is as the past, it is called born. *It is of the Holy Spirit.* The Holy Spirit is called God, and the gift of God, and charity; and charity alone made him to be incarnate.

VERS. 21.-- *She shall bring forth.* Lest Joseph should seem not to be necessary to her, he adds: *She shall bring forth.* And so thou shalt be necessary for her care. *And thou shalt call his name Jesus.* He says the same to this man which he had foretold to Mary, that from the utterance he may set before men as well as women that the promised Saviour has already come. *For he.* The name is interpreted.

VERS. 22.-- *Now this,* etc. That she was espoused to a kinsman: that she was found with child: that a virgin brought forth: that he was called Jesus: that he saves. For the Evangelist says this when all things had already been [0071D] fulfilled.

*That it might be fulfilled.* The prophecy of Isaiah is a sign of the foreknowledge of God, because what it says is certainly foreknown by God: and therefore it ought to be feared by man. But no sign effects what it designates: but only signifies what it shows, so prophecy does not make a necessity of those things which it foretells, but is a sign of the foreknowledge of God.

[n: (HIER.)] There is no necessity of things from the utterance of the prophets, but only the showing forth of truth. Prophecy did not make a necessity of those things which it says, but is a sign of the foreknowledge of God.

One prophecy is from the predestination of God, which must in all ways come to pass, so that it is fulfilled without our [0072A] choice: as is this of which we here treat. Another is from the foreknowledge of God, with which our choice is mingled. Another there is which is called a threatening, which is made for a sign of divine punishment, that the elect may flee from the face of the bow, and the incautious justly perish; and this not from foreknowledge: because a thing is known far otherwise than it is threatened as to come.

VERS. 23.-- *Behold a virgin.* The prophet Isaiah marvels, and as it were rousing all from sleep, says: *Behold a virgin shall be with child [n: (Isa. VII)]*. To the Holy Spirit that was present which in time was not yet. *Behold a virgin,* etc. The Jews say that this is not a name of integrity, but of age, a girl. But how then is it a sign? He follows the sense of Isaiah, not the words. In place of "she shall conceive" he sets down: *She shall be with child:* and "they shall call" for "thou shalt call," [0072B] or "he shall be called."

*Emmanuel.* It is proper to Christ, as is Jesus, because he abides always with those whom he saves, by helping them.

For three causes he supports from the Old Testament the things which he sets down in the Gospel: for testification, that he may have testimony from the law and the prophets: for the confirmation of faith, because we believe more easily when we see fulfilled the things which were foretold: for the joining of the New and the Old Testament.



## CHAPTER ONE. (cont.)

VERS. 24.-- *And Joseph rising up,* etc. [n: (BEDA.)] Morally. Whosoever is moved by God, let him break off delays, let him rise from sleep: let him do what is commanded. *He did as he had commanded.* Perfect obedience. He did not only what the angel commanded, but also as he commanded. Obedient by the showing of service and by the effect of love, he is rightly said [0072C] to have done as he commanded him. *The angel of the Lord.* No place is left for lying, where the office of angels is performed. *And he took his wife,* etc. To avoid the infamy of the virgin, to conceal the coming of the Saviour, for the necessary service of the child at his birth.

VERS. 25.-- *Till she brought forth.* Not that afterwards, which is the more certain: since in many ways he knew that he who was born was God.

Not that he knew her afterwards: but *till* is set for *and,* or for *for ever,* as: *Till I make thy enemies the footstool of thy feet [n: (Psal. CIX)]*. It is said that Joseph could not see Mary face to face, whom the Holy Spirit had wholly filled from the conception. And therefore he did not know face to face her whom he had espoused, until the womb was emptied: [0072D] of which there is no question here. *The firstborn,* etc. Everything is called firstborn which opens the womb, whether another follow or not. Or the firstborn among all the elect by grace. But properly he is called the only-begotten of God the Father, or of Mary.



## CHAPTER II.

VERS. 1.-- *When therefore he was born,* etc. Although Matthew passes over the nativity, yet in relating the coming of the Magi he briefly commemorates it, saying thus: *When therefore. [n: (RAB.)]* Four things are here set down, confirmed by the prophets, the nativity, the name, the place and the time, etc., *as far as* of the coming of the Magi Luke is silent, and Matthew sets it forth.

[0073A] *Bethlehem of Juda.* To distinguish it from that which is in Galilee, in the tribe of Zabulon. For there are two Bethlehems: Bethlehem was formerly called Ephratha; Bethlehem is the house of bread, because there the living Bread was to be born, who came down from heaven, who is laid in a manger: that having fed the irrational he may make them fellows of the angels. But it signifies the Church, which is the house in which the living bread is eaten.

*In the days. [n: (HIER.)]* He sets this down not only for the time, but that it may be seen fulfilled, etc., *as far as* the Jews point out the place: the time of the coming they do not know.

[n: (AUG.)] Jesus was made manifest not to the learned nor to the just: for it prevails, etc., *as far as* that no great man might be proud, no weak man despair.

[0073B] *They came.* The Magi, not after a year: because then he would not be found in the manger, but in Egypt, but on the thirteenth day. But they were from the land of the Persians, where also is the river Saba, from which the region is named, near which is Arabia also, where the Magi were kings. Who, although they are said to have offered three gifts, are not on that account proved not to have been more than three; but that through them the Gentiles which were born of the three sons of Noe, and were to come to the faith, might be prefigured: or there were so many princes, who led many in their train. Therefore the Magi make their request chiefly at Jerusalem: because through Balaam they had heard that he was to be born of Israel. For a new star was showing forth a new man. The star is Christ, whom we ought to follow, who unless he arise in our hearts, the king of the Jews is not sought in the East.

[0073C]VERS. 2.-- *Where is he that is born king,* etc. It is the confusion of the Jews, when they learn the nativity of Christ from the Gentiles, and if they do not believe, they are without excuse. *For we have seen his star.* This star, the herald of the Lord's nativity, never appeared before, but the child then created it and assigned it to the Magi: which soon, its office performed, ceased to be. A mute star proclaims Christ not yet speaking; afterwards, when he spoke, the apostles announced him to the Jews, as to those using reason; a rational substance, that is, an angel, announced the birth of Christ. But an irrational thing, that is, a star, led the Magi, the firstfruits of the Gentiles, not yet using reason. To the shepherds angels, to the Magi a star, yet to both the tongue of the heavens speaks, because the tongue of the prophets was already ceasing. Whether the star arose in the east, or whether [0073D] they, being placed there, saw it risen toward the west, is doubtful. For it could arise in the east, and lead them to Jerusalem. But while they seek human help, as it were from the law, they are forsaken by the divine. By the star they understood that he was born in Judaea, and therefore they come to Jerusalem, where, learning the place and then setting out upon their journey, they first have the star going before them, which they recognize.

Allegorically. The star is the illumination of faith which leads to Christ. While they turn aside to the Jews, they lose it: because while they seek counsel from the wicked, they lose the true illumination.

[n: (LEO.)] Three men follow the leading of the light from above, accompanying with intent contemplation the token of the brightness that went before them, [0074A] to the acknowledgment of the truth, etc., *as far as* that the mystery of so great a vision might not lie hidden from them, and that what was shown to their eyes as unwonted might not be obscure to their minds.

VERS. 3.-- *But Herod hearing,* etc. He is called king, that by comparison with him who is sought, this one may be understood a stranger, because the proper one had already failed.

*But Herod hearing.* That another king of the Jews than himself was sought; for, being a foreigner, he wished to seem the lawful king: and therefore he burned the records in which the genealogy is woven.

*He was troubled,* etc. Either because he fears the end of his kingdom, or on account of the wrath of the Romans if he should allow this, who had decreed that no one should be called king or lord without their counsel. The king of heaven being born, the king of earth [0074B] was troubled, because assuredly earthly height is confounded when heavenly loftiness is proclaimed.

*With him.* Because of favour: because often the people the more unjustly favour those whom they endure as cruel. Whence Solomon: *A king* unjust *has all his ministers wicked [n: (Prov. XXIX)]*. [var: Vulg. Prov. 29:12 reads *Princeps qui libenter audit verba mendacii, omnes ministros habet impios*, "A prince that gladly heareth lying words hath all his servants wicked"; Migne's *Rex* stands where the received text has *Princeps*, and *injustus*, set in roman between his italics, is his own supplied word]

VERS. 4.-- *And assembling all the chief priests.* Note the diligence of the inquirer, that if he should find him he might do what he afterwards showed himself to wish: but if not, that he might be excused to the Romans. He was also probing whether their king would make the Jews sad or glad. *Where Christ should be born.* From the Jews he asks the place, from the Magi the time, that he may be made certain of both.

VERS. 5.-- *In Bethlehem of Juda.* They express the place of the nativity, which by the testimony of Scripture [0074C] they had learned, so that their very knowledge might become for them a testimony of damnation, for us a help to faith.

From this it is clear that not from ignorance, but from hardness of heart, they refused to believe.

VERS. 6.-- *And thou, Bethlehem.* He sets this down as it was said by them, because although they do not set down the words, they do in some manner set down the truth of the sense.

VERS. 7.-- *The Magi being called privately.* The priests and scribes being removed; for he feared lest the Jews should hide the promised one as by an oracle of God, if they should perceive that he wished to destroy him. Therefore also he promised that he would adore him, lest any should perceive his guile: but that without suspicion, for the favour of his good will, they might bring him word.

VERS. 8.-- *That I may adore him.* Herod promises [0074D] devotion, but sharpens the sword: painting the malice of his heart with the colour of humility. He feigned by countenance and by words to adore him whom with envious mind he was planning to kill. Whose person the hypocrites represent, who seek God feignedly, and never deserve to find him.

VERS. 9.-- *And behold the star which they had seen.* Having entered Judaea they are forsaken by the token of the star, that they may be compelled to inquire from the law. Or they who seek human help are forsaken by the divine. Nor was it fitting that a sign given to unbelievers should appear to those of the household of the law and the prophets; because, *if they hear not Moses and the prophets: neither if one from the dead,* etc. It did not keep the paths of the upper air: but being very near the house, otherwise they would not have distinguished the house.

[0075A]Morally. The star is a good exhortation leading to Christ. Or rather faith, which is the illumination of the mind, through which he who enters sees Christ, who is the morning star: and having seen him he rejoices with joy and does not cease to adore.

VERS. 10.-- *They rejoiced with a great joy,* etc. He rejoices with joy who rejoices for the sake of God (who is the true joy). He adds also "great," than which nothing is greater. And "they rejoiced exceedingly," because of a great thing one man can rejoice more, another less.

VERS. 11. *And entering the house,* etc. Three Magi come by one journey to adore God: because in the one Christ (who is the way) the inseparable Trinity was to be adored by them. *The child with Mary his mother,* etc. Often is he named a child, that they may recognize him of whom [0075B] it was said: *A child is born to us.* [var: Vulg. Isa. 9:6 reads *Parvulus enim natus est nobis*, "For a little one is born to us"; Migne prints *Puer*, which is the very word the gloss is expounding]

Why was not Joseph also found with Mary by the Magi? Lest any occasion of evil suspicion should thence be given to the Gentiles, who sent their firstfruits to adore him as soon as the Saviour was born.

*They adored him.* Thus confessing him God, whom they understand to have been brought to be man, and about to die, which they show by the myrrh.

*And opening,* etc. They testify their faith by mystical gifts: the gifts closed are the faith of the heart; the gifts opened, etc., *as far as* or by these three there are intimated in the same Christ royal power, divine majesty, human mortality.

VERS. 12.-- *And having received an answer.* As Moses, being silent, [0075C] cried out, so these with devout affection were asking what the divine will might command. This answer is not made through an angel, but through God himself, because no other appointed the way of return, save he who says: *I am the way, the truth, and the life.* The child does not speak to them, lest the divinity be revealed before the time, and that the true humanity may be held. Whence also he is soon sent into Egypt: because faith had to be nourished unto the reward, and the life of doctrine must be prepared for the going. *By another way,* etc. In this a pattern is given to believers, that they may come devoutly to God: and that they may attend to what he commands, namely, that they return not to the devil: but that they may come by the paths of the virtues to their country, and that they who fell by despising may rise again by obeying.

[n: (LEO.)] They adore in the flesh the Word, in infancy wisdom, [0075D] in weakness power, and in the truth of man the Lord of majesty, etc., *as far as* because what was proper in the substances was not diverse in the person.

VERS. 13.-- *Take the child,* etc. [n: (HILAR.)] When he was signifying that she was espoused to a just man, he called her wife; but after the birth she is shown only as the mother of Jesus, so that, as to the just Joseph the marriage with Mary was reckoned in virginity, so her venerable virginity as a mother might be shown in Jesus.

VERS. 14, 15.-- *Who rising up.* Joseph is a figure of the preachers, who bore Christ, with his mother, that is, the faith of Christ and of the Church, to the Gentiles, Herod being left behind, that is, the unbelief of the Jews. *By night.* Because [0076A] secretly by flight he went down to enlighten Egypt, night being left to the Jews.

By night he bore him into Egypt, because in the night of ignorance he left them to those unbelieving ones from whom he himself withdrew. When he returns, no mention is made of night, because at the end of the world the Jews, receiving the faith as though Christ returning from Egypt, shall be enlightened.

*Into Egypt, and he was there,* etc. He shows [Egypt] venerating a God of every kind: because Christ, not received by the Jews, passes over by preaching to the Gentiles. He fled into Egypt as he was born, that he might repair corrupted nature. So he fled, that he might call back the fugitives. That he fled was a matter of sacrament, not of fear, that he might give his own an example of fleeing. He did not flee death, who had come to die: nor did he dread the snares, who had come to lay open the craft [0076B] of the devil. Of this flight Isaiah foretold: *Behold the Lord shall ascend upon a light cloud,* that is, flesh without sin: *and shall enter into Egypt [n: (Isa. XIX)]*. But for seven years he lay hid in Egypt.

*Out of Egypt I have called.* This is found in Osee according to the Hebrew verity: or in the book of Numbers, as some assert: because the whole was done by the disposition of God.

VERS. 16.-- *Then Herod seeing.* It is likely that, since nothing had been reported to Herod by the Magi, he believed that they had been deceived by a false star, and had therefore not returned to him: whence also he rested so long from the search for the child. Then, when the things which had been done or said in the temple were made public, he perceived that he had been mocked by the Magi, and hastening to the death of Christ he slew the children.

[0076C]It is likely that for a year and four days from the nativity of Christ Herod raged against the children: which perhaps he deferred for this reason, that he set out for Rome, or was accused there, or that he might consult the Romans concerning those things which were said about Christ. Perhaps therefore he held himself back so long from the search for the child, that he might apprehend him the more carefully, and that he might not be able to slip away in any manner.

*He slew all the children.* As soon as Christ appeared to the world, persecution began against him: which prefigured the persecution of the saints: and while the infant is sought, infants are slain; in whom the form of martyrdom is born, where the infancy of the Church is consecrated.

The death of the little ones figures the passion of all the martyrs, who were slain as little ones, humble and innocent: who suffered not in Judaea only, but everywhere [0076D] at the hands of the wicked, whom Herod signifies. That they were two years old: because they were perfect in doctrine and in work. Those being slain, Christ escaped: because bodies can be destroyed, the divinity cannot be touched.



## CHAPTER II. (cont.)

*And in all the borders thereof.* He was not content with the devastation of Bethlehem, but laid waste the neighbouring places; nor had he any mercy for age, from a son of one night to a son of two years, but that he slew them all.

*From two years old.* Therefore from two years old, that as Herod had taken in beforehand the borders of the city, so also he might take in beforehand another year. Therefore also from two years old: because he feared lest the child, whom the stars served, should fashion for himself an appearance a little above or below his age.

[0077A]VERS. 17.-- *Then was fulfilled.* It is called fulfilled: because before it came to pass it was but half-full to those who read it, since what sounded in the letter secretly promised something to come.

[n: (CHRYSOST.)] He says that the star appeared for a year, as in the destruction of the Romans signs appeared in heaven, when the voice of the angels was heard: Let us pass over from these seats.

VERS. 18.-- *A voice in Rama.* That is, in a high place it was spread far and wide.

Allegorically. Or, the voice of the Church groaning over the slaughter of her members ascends to the throne of the judge on high. *A voice in Rama.* On account of the Levite's wife, destroyed by fornication and divided into twelve parts according to the number of the tribes, all Israel [0077B] destroyed the tribe of Benjamin save three hundred men: the weeping and wailing of those who survived was heard as far as Rama, which is a place near Gabaa, at the twelfth milestone from Bethlehem. *Was heard.* He heightens it, so that hyperbolically Rachel, already dead, is said with the feeling of one grieving to be already weeping for her sons. Whence by this the history concerning the Chaldeans is woven, that the devastation to come from them upon the people of the Jews would be like to the former disaster. But more truly, the Spirit revealing it through the evangelist, the prophecy is taken of the slaughter of the children. He says therefore that what was spoken was then completed, because although the word of the prophecy looks to the impending captivity, yet in it, as in a shadow, the future truth of the slaughter of the infants is proclaimed.

*Rachel.* Because she was buried near Bethlehem, and from [0077C] the earthly lodging of her body received the name of mother. Or because many of Benjamin and Joseph were slain. Of Rachel was Benjamin born, to whose lot Bethlehem does not belong, but only to the tribe of Judah. But because Judah and Benjamin are neighbouring tribes in the borders of Bethlehem, many also of the tribe of Benjamin were slain.

Note that the figure of the sacrament is better intimated through Rachel (than if Bethlehem were said to have wept), because through her in all things the pattern of the Church is commended, which weeps not so much for those carried off by death as for those destroyed by torment. *Rachel.* That is, the Church, weeps for her tender lambs destroyed: neither will she be comforted in the present, because they are not: but she sends forward all her hope and consolation to the eternal life.

The Church weeps, and will not be comforted here: because [0077D] her sons are not of this world. Or she weeps: because while she brings forth, she has justice [sic: justitiam], whence it is said: *You shall weep,* etc., but a consolation is added: *Your sorrow shall be turned into joy [n: (Joan. XVI)]*.

VERS. 19.-- *But Herod being dead, behold,* etc. Because, the perfidy of the Jews being lulled to sleep, and Elias and Enoch preaching, Judaea shall receive the word of God.

The king being dead, his accomplices straightway perish, so, the persecution of the Church ceasing, she is invited to heavenly things.

VERS. 20.-- *Into the land.* He does not determine into what part, so that, Joseph doubting, the angel may return: and that by his frequent address Joseph may be made the more certain. Because he did not distinguish into what part, therefore Josephus understood Judaea, which was the worthier part of the kingdom. *They are dead.* [0078A] Some relate that Herod caused the nobler of the Jews to be slain over his own funeral, that he might so compel the Jews to weep for his death.

VERS. 21.-- *Who rising up.* Allegorically. Joseph bears the figure of the apostles, by whose office Christ is carried about. The apostles came first into the land of Israel: because they preached first to the Jews. But because of Herod, that is, the hereditary unbelief remaining, they fear and withdraw, being admonished to preach grace to the Gentiles, and to carry Christ over to them.

The land of Israel being named, it seemed to Joseph that such a child ought to dwell nowhere but in Jerusalem, where the temple was and the celebration of the prophets. Yet the angel wished Galilee to be understood, which the Jews also inhabited, which shows that it had thus been predestined, [0078B] because he shall be called a Nazarene.

VERS. 22.-- *He feared to go thither.* If he feared Judaea on account of Archelaus, the heir of his father's cruelty, why not Galilee also, where another Herod, his brother, was reigning? Because Archelaus after his father obtained the sole rule of the whole kingdom: but growing insolent he was cast down by Tiberius Caesar into exile at Lyons, and then the kingdom was divided into four tetrarchies, one of which, that is Galilee, Herod his brother obtained.

It is asked: why did Joseph not fear to go into Galilee as into Judaea, since Archelaus reigned there also? But he could better lie hid in Nazareth (which was remote) than in Jerusalem, where was the head of the kingdom and Archelaus constantly present.

*He withdrew into the parts.* That Christ is not carried over thither [0078C] where Archelaus was reigning signifies that Christ shall be hidden from those in whom Antichrist shall reign.

VERS. 23.-- *Nazareth.* Nazareth is interpreted *a new shoot* or *the flower of the field*, from the root of which shoot the holy of holies is read to have ascended, to signify the substance of his eternity. As therefore he chose the time in which he should be born and the place, so also the city in which he should grow up: whose name is a token that he who is holiness itself, nurtured in holiness, is rightly called the holy of holies: whence also his disciples were first called Nazaraeans, but afterwards from Christ were called Christians.

Nazareth of Galilee, whither he is carried over, signifies that part of the same nation which was to receive the faith: whence it is interpreted *a flower*: because the more ardently the Church passes over from earthly things to heavenly, the more it abounds in the flower and shoot [0078D] of the virtues.

*By the prophets.* He says prophets in the plural, because we have no fixed instance from Scripture: he shows that he took the sense, not the words. Or in the same words in Isaiah according to the Hebrew verity: *A Nazarene shall ascend from his root [n: (Isa. XI)]*.



## CHAPTER III.

VERS. 1.-- *In those days.* He passes over many things, and crosses to the preaching of John. *In those days.* He takes in not the years of boyhood only, but all of them up to the preaching of John, that is, when he was nearly thirty years old. Luke expresses the times more exactly: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar. *Preaching.* He who had before kept silence made himself known by baptizing, preparing the way [0079A] for the Lord. *In the desert of Judaea.* Because the Jews had been deserted by God, and for them repentance is necessary, that they may return.

VERS. 2.-- *Repentance.* The herald announces this, which afterwards the Truth announces through himself; repentance goes before, the promise of the kingdom follows: he who truly repents, in himself his past errors, then lifts up his mind to the heavenly kingdom. If remission is made freely in baptism, why is repentance preached? But the manner of repentance is threefold. The first, to renounce and condemn errors and all evils before baptism: which is necessary for those who are coming to Christ. The second, that those who have fallen after baptism be called back through repentance. The third, whereby the saints are daily cleansed of such sins as life is not lived without.

[0079B]To repent is to weep for things done before, and not to commit what must be wept for. The kingdom of heaven is said to be at hand for the penitent. Not earthly things, as in the old law: and this through the obedience of Christ. And John first preached this kingdom of heaven: *Do penance.* The first virtue is, through repentance to slay the old man, and to hate vices: and he who does not do this not only fails to lay hold of the virtues, but does not even escape punishments. The virtue of repentance is conceived by fear, which is the beginning of wisdom. Repentance is from punishing, whereby each man punishes what he has unlawfully committed.

To do penance is to make fruits worthy of repentance. *The kingdom of heaven.* That is, Christ, through whom the saints reign in the heavenly places. Or the Gospel, by which he invites to the kingdom.

[0079C] *For it hath drawn near,* etc. Unless it had drawn near, no one could return: because the weak and the blind were without the way (which is Christ): and John, preparing that way, sets it before the penitent.

VERS. 3.-- *The voice of one crying.* John is the voice, Christ the word, who cries in John: No word is heard without a voice, nor is a voice of any avail without the understanding of the word. The voice prepares the way for the word, that it may be received. Whence: *I have prepared a lamp for my Christ [n: (Psal. CXXXI)]*.

*In the desert.* A pattern for the penitent: the place of his converse is not the throng of men, but the desert. His clothing is not soft to the point of looseness, but rough: his food scanty and unaccustomed.

Typically, the desert signifies the life of the saints, set apart from the enticements of the world.

[0079D] *The way of the Lord.* The way of the Lord is made straight to the heart, when his word is diligently heard.

VERS. 4.-- *And John himself.* He who preaches repentance displays the habit of repentance. In him the meanness of clothing and of food is praised, the use of which in the rich man is called to account.

And John himself instructs the penitent in his own person, and sets forth a pattern of life by dwelling in the desert, living on locusts, clothing himself in camel's hair.

The servant of God ought not to have clothing for adornment or for delight, but only for covering nakedness. Hence John was clothed in hair.

VERS. 5.-- *Then there went out to him,* etc. Because unless a man go out from evils, he is not washed. Whence it fitly follows: *They were baptized by him in the Jordan:* which is interpreted *a going down*, [0080A] because they were going down from the pride of the old man to the humility of confession and amendment. For already then an example was given to those about to be baptized, of confessing sins and promising better things.

VERS. 6.-- *In the Jordan.* Because in it the figure of baptism went before, and from its name it requires a going down from pride, which is fitting for the baptized. *Confessing.* The confession of sins is the testimony of a conscience that fears God. For he who fears the judgment of God is not ashamed to confess his sins. More perfectly, fear looses every shame. The confession of sin has shame in it, and that blushing is itself a heavy punishment. And therefore we are bidden to confess our sins, that we may suffer the blushing for a punishment. For this very thing is part of the divine judgment.

VERS. 7.-- *Many of the Pharisees,* etc. These are of the [0080B] heretics of the Jews, and the Pharisees set the righteousness of observances and traditions before all else. Whence also they are called Pharisees, that is, divided from the people by a private righteousness. The Sadducees, that is, the just: for they claim for themselves what they are not: these deny the resurrection, saying that the soul perishes with the body: they receive the five books of Moses, they reject the prophets. These, when they come to baptism, John rebukes: because they most of all had need of correction and repentance.

*Brood of vipers,* etc., that is, poisoned sons of the poisoned: because they envy the good and persecute them, they wound their neighbors as their fathers did.

The viper kills its own father, so the Jews killed the prophets who were their fathers.

VERS. 8.-- *Bring forth therefore fruits worthy. [n: (BEDA.)]* [var: Vulg. Mt 3:8 *fructum dignum*, singular; the plural *fructus dignos* is Lc 3:8's] [0080C] As if he were saying: Why do you not first lay aside your poisons, that so to baptism, etc., *as far as* it is grace that feels, and feeling seeks holiness.

VERS. 9.-- *For I say.* He draws them back from the flesh, that they may consider the works of God's predestination. The first are the rudiments of faith, to believe that God can do whatever he will, so that he who created all things out of nothing can form sons of Abraham from stones or from dust. *Of stones.* Pointing to those stones which Josue caused to be carried over out of the Jordan, toward which he says this as though stretching out his finger.

Josue caused twelve stones to be carried from the midst of the Jordan onto dry land, and others to be set in their place out of the land in the same channel: by which the blinding of the Jews and the transforming of the Gentiles to the light are foresignified.

[0080D]Or he calls the Gentiles stones: and the sense is: Do not glory in the seed of the flesh: because these only are the sons of God who have been enlightened by grace and inwardly raised up. He says "raise up" pointedly, because Christ received Sara, that is, the Church, and raises up sons of Abraham by grace, he having died without children, lest so great a patriarch should be deprived of the promises. In presage of this thing God once begot a son of Sara.

VERS. 10.-- *For now the axe.* But lest they should seem free of danger if they kept themselves apart from such sacraments, he threatens. *The axe.* Christ, who consists of haft and iron, that is, of the humanity by which he is held, and the divinity because he cuts. *Is laid:* because although he waits through patience, he yet sees what he is about to do. [0081A] *To the root.* That is, the end of the Jewish people, that he may take away from the land of the living those who do not believe in Christ. Or, the axe is the sentence of judgment, or the preaching of the Gospel. *To the root.* Note, not to the branches, but to the root. For when the sons of the wicked are taken away, what else is cut off but the branches of an unfruitful tree? When the whole offspring is taken away together with the parent, the tree is cut off at the root, that nothing may remain from which some shoot might spring up again. The roots are thoughts, by which men, being planted, are either lifted up on high to heaven, or sent down to the depths of hell. The tree is the human race: of this tree some branches are dry, that is, the pagans, fit for the burning. Others are green, but without fruit: as the hypocrites, who make a show of holiness, but are empty within: others are fruitful, but poisonous, that is, the heretics: who by preaching [0081B] bring forth fruit, but a deadly fruit. Others, that is, the catholics, who bear good fruit. *Every tree therefore,* as the Gentiles, the hypocrites, who bear none, and the heretics, who bear evil fruit.

VERS. 11.-- *I indeed.* Lest he should seem to threaten on his own authority, he begins to disclose of how great dignity he is: whose presence he holds out as a threat, or whose benefit he urges upon them: *I indeed baptize you in water.* I only wash bodies, because I cannot loose sins, so that as I run before in being born and in preaching, so I do in baptizing: that I may direct to the baptism of Christ the penitent, whom I mark off by this sign from the impenitent. *He who is to come after me.* And though I admonish you to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, to cast away pride: yet I cannot loose from sins. *He is mightier than I.* Because I baptize unto [0081C] repentance, he unto remission. I have the Spirit, he gives it. I preach the kingdom of heaven, he gives it.

*Whose I am not,* etc. Others write: Whose I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his shoe. Now John could have said both, either in one continuous speech or at different times: so that one evangelist took up this, another that. Yet all of them told the truth. His aim in this is to show the excellence of Christ and his own humility.

Or according to the allegory. The shoe is the mystery of the incarnation; the latchet, the tying of the mystery. Therefore John is not able to loose the latchet, because he does not suffice to search out the mystery of the incarnation. Or, I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his shoe, [0081D] that is, I do not usurp for myself the name of bridegroom, nor do I wish to be believed or called the bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom. For it was the custom that if any man refused to take to wife her who fell to him, the man who should come forward as bridegroom to her by right of kinship would loose his shoe. John therefore, who is not the bridegroom, says: I am not worthy, etc. As if he were to say: I cannot uncover the footsteps of the Redeemer: because I do not usurp for myself the name of bridegroom.

Or he simply humbles himself, or he is not worthy to carry about the sacraments of the Gospel by preaching, which was not assigned to him but committed to the apostles. I am not worthy to unfold the nature of the Divinity to the humanity. Or, I am not worthy to bear [0082A] the preaching of the Gospel, or to usurp the name of bridegroom. John, as a mere man, could not give the Spirit, by whom guilt is remitted. But Christ gives it, because he is God: and he baptizes in the word, of which it is said: *And you are clean by reason of the word which I have spoken to you [n: (Joan. XV)]* [var: Vulg. Jo 15:3 *Jam vos mundi estis propter sermonem quem locutus sum vobis*]; and elsewhere: *Cleansing them by the laver of water in the word of sanctified life [n: (Ephes. V)]* [var: Vulg. Eph 5:26 *ut illam sanctificaret, mundans lavacro aquae in verbo vitae*, without *eos* and *sanctificatae*].

*In the Holy Spirit.* Either in the spirit of sanctification, and in fire, that is, in the proving of tribulation. Or in the spirit he washes in the present: afterwards, if any stain has crept in, he will burn it away to purity by the fire of purgatory: which is to be believed of the lighter sins. Whence in Leviticus, upon the altar a fire sent down from heaven burned continually, that is, the fire of divine love, which as it were rebaptizes all those in Christ (that is, those who are offered upon the altar) and burns away [0082B] the vices of their flesh.

VERS.12.-- *Whose fan.* The fan in his hand is the sifting of judgment by which are distinguished the light and those empty of the fruit of good work. *In his hand,* because the Father judges no man, but has given all judgment to the Son. *He shall thoroughly cleanse,* that is, he daily cleanses from divers temptations. Or, *He shall thoroughly cleanse,* when for manifest sins the perverse man is cast out of the Church, or after death is damned. *But the chaff.* The chaff springs from the same origin as the wheat, that is, from the seed, but the cockle from a different one. The chaff, therefore, are those who are steeped in the sacraments of the faith, but are not solid: the cockle are those who are severed from the elect both in work and in profession. Of these it is said: *He that believeth not is already judged,* and therefore no mention is made here of them. *Unquenchable.* Because it shall not [0082C] be quenched, neither shall it quench those it torments, but shall punish them eternally. And it is so called by way of distinction from that fire of which it is said: *Thou hast tried us by fire [n: (Psal. LXV)]*, etc.



## CHAPTER III. (cont.)

VERS. 13.-- *Then he came.* When John was preaching and baptizing, namely when Jesus was thirty years old, showing that no one ought to be made a priest or a preacher save at a serviceable age. As Joseph at thirty took up the rule of Egypt. David began his reign at that age: Ezekiel merited the gift of prophecy. Jesus came for these causes, that he might approve the baptism of John, and that (because he was man) he might fulfil all righteousness and the humility of the law: and that, sanctifying the waters, he might show through the dove the coming of the Holy Spirit in the laver. For he came not out of any need [0082D] of washing, but that no one, however holy, should judge the grace of baptism superfluous. *From Galilee to the Jordan.* Galilee, a passing over: the Jordan, a going down. He therefore who wishes to be baptized, let him pass over from vices, and going down, let him be humbled.

VERS. 15.-- *Suffer it now.* Suffer me now to be baptized by thee, that afterwards thou mayest be baptized in the Spirit with that which thou seekest of me. For as it is fitting to give an example of fulfilling all righteousness, that all may learn that no one is perfect without the water of baptism.

*Then he suffered him.* When he had come to know that righteousness was to be fulfilled in such an order. He suffered him, because that is true humility which its companion obedience does not desert.

The Spirit taught him in a moment what he had not known before, [0083A] and therefore what he had before humbly feared, he devoutly fulfilled.

VERS. 16.-- *And being baptized.* Christ sanctified the waters of baptism: because it belongs to him whose it is to create, to sanctify also.

As man consists of two things, that is, of body and of soul, so he is reborn of two: of water, which cleanses filth and buries him together with Christ: and of the fire of the Spirit, by whose blaze we are caught up to heaven. So the Church after baptism reaches after the summit of the virtues by certain increases, as Christ when baptized came up out of the water. So after baptism those go up who advance to the virtues: and those who before were carnal and sons of Adam become spiritual and sons of God.

*They were opened,* etc. And this too belongs to the fulfilling of righteousness. [0083B] For not then for the first time did the heavenly things lie open to him, nor was the Holy Spirit then given: but he showed that to us, through the baptism we have received, the entrance of heaven lies open, and that the Holy Spirit is given. For that the heavens were opened, that the Holy Spirit came, that the voice of the Father sounded, etc., these mystical things are within us.

The entrance into heaven lies open to the reborn through Christ, which through Adam had been closed.

*As a dove.* He had a true body, formed for the hour, in the appearance of a dove: because otherwise the Spirit could not be seen by men as a dove, not because it was a true dove, but because the Spirit was in a bodily appearance, yet was not itself a body. So of this figure it is judged as of the others in which God appeared: which, their office fulfilled, were dissolved. Fitly the Spirit came down in a dove, [0083C] which is simple and gentle, that he might point out both the simplicity of his own nature, and him upon whom he was descending, the meek herald and giver of mercy. In like manner all who are reborn by baptism ought to be filled with the seven virtues signified in the dove. The dove is a stranger to the malice of gall, in which we are forbidden anger. It wounds none with beak or claws, in which innocence is marked. Nor does it fall upon the smallest little birds, on which other birds feed themselves and their young: in which we are forbidden robbery. It feeds on clean grain: in which abstinence is marked, it cherishes the young of others as its own, behold charity. It gives a moan for a song, behold compunction. It sits above the waters, that by the shadow foreseen in the waters it may turn aside from the hawk: behold watchfulness. In a dove the Spirit appeared above the Lord: because he came to gather us through meekness. [0083D] Above the disciples in fire, whom he was coming to kindle against their own selves for the consuming of the rust of sin. Adam by sinning lost heaven, Christ appeared glorified by the Holy Spirit through the dove: the quivering flame which barred the way, the water of baptism quenched: because water is contrary to fire.

*I am well pleased.* That is, I have established my good pleasure, that thou, in whom is nothing but good, mayest please, and that through thee others may please, not in themselves, but in thee, that is, united to thee by faith and brightness.



## CHAPTER IV.

VERS. 1.-- *Then Jesus.* After baptism, because there is no delay before temptation: that he may straightway teach the baptized [0084A] to go out of the world, and in quiet to be free for God: so the sons of Israel after the passage of the sea go up through the desert, and eat manna until they come to the land of promise. *Then Jesus was led,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] This is the order of right converse, that after receiving the grace of the Holy Spirit we should gird ourselves the more closely against the devil: by that way the Samaritan came down, because clothed in flesh he bore the same temptations.

*To the Spirit*, the Holy, who sends strong to the battle those whom he fills. Without this Spirit, he who goes to the battle quickly falls. *That he might be tempted by the devil.* He is not tempted by the devil save because he has gone out to the desert, that is, has begun to be zealous for good.

VERS. 2.-- *And when he had fasted. [n: (BEDA.)]* He fasts that he may be tempted, he is tempted because he fasts, and he gives us an example of fasting, [0084B] etc., *as far as* and so, as long as we are here, let us always bewail our sins: because by this number the present life is shown.

[n: (LEO.)] While through the various actions of this life our solicitude is stretched out, it must needs be that from the dust of the world, etc., *as far as* that we, who have been raised together in his resurrection, may be found to have died together in his passion.

*Afterwards he was hungry.* This belongs to true humanity: and through this comes the occasion of tempting. The power lies hidden, the weakness lies open.

VERS. 3.-- *And coming.* Because hunger is a sign of weakness. And so temptation is not wanting to us in abstinence. Through the outward weakness he tempts Christ, in whom he found no law of sin. *If thou be the Son [0084C] of God.* It is one thing to be a man exploring these matters, another to be a man tempting, while he seems to confess God and endeavors to mock at one of this kind. For so he tempts, that he may explore what he fears. So he explores, that by tempting he may deceive. *If thou be the Son of God.* He had known that the Son of God had come into the world, whether by the prophets, or by the angels announcing it, or by John pointing him out: but because he saw humble things in him, what he had suspected concerning the Godhead came into doubt with him out of pride. Whence also he cunningly makes inquiry: Nor was it unworthy that Christ, who had come to be slain, should be tempted, that by overcoming temptations he might give us the power of overcoming temptations, as by his own death he took away our mortality.

[n: (RAB.)] Christ did not suffer himself to be tempted except after baptism, hinting that those who come to him will suffer heavier things, [0084D] etc., *as far as* but Christ was tempted by suggestion only: because the delight of sin did not bite his mind.

VERS. 4.-- *It is written.* He does not use his power, but the authority of the Scriptures, teaching us to fight rather with doctrine than with miracles. *Not in bread alone doth man live.* As if to say: Thy persuasion is a temptation: because thou treatest of the food of the body, and not of the food of the mind. The lower part of man is sustained by bread, the other is refreshed by the word of God: but because thou treatest of the lower part, it is plain that thou art a tempter. *But in every word,* etc. Every word is charity, in which are fulfilled all the things that proceed out of the mouth of God, because by whosesoever ministry they are spoken, they are not his but God's: but if anything contrary is inserted, this is not [0085A] of God. Out of the one word, that is, the wisdom of God, proceeds whatever the saints speak, who are his mouth.

VERS. 5.-- *Then he took him.* The first and the last temptation were in the desert; the middle one, moreover, was historically the last, after he had returned to Jerusalem. Because Matthew follows not the order of the history, but the order of Adam's temptation: whereas Luke follows the order in which the thing was done.

Because he was left conquered and uncertain by Christ's answer: after the first he went on to the second temptation.

That he permitted himself to be taken up was not weakness, but patience: whereas in the devil it was not power, but pride.

Note that all these things were accomplished by the bodily senses. Nor is it a wonder if he permitted himself to be carried about: if the taking up is so [0085B] understood, he who permitted himself to be crucified.

*Upon the pinnacle. [n: (RAB.)]* In Palestine the roofs were flat on top, and there was the seat of the teachers, whence, etc., *as far as* he shows that we should obey whoever commands good and lofty things, but resist him who wills to cast us down.

*If thou be the Son. [n: (BEDA.)]* In all the temptations he does this, that he may understand, etc., *as far as* it is likely that the devil appeared in the shape of a man.

*Cast thyself.* This voice befits him who busies himself to cast all men down: in which he is shown to be weak, because he can hurt no one, unless that man first cast himself down. For he was suggesting that by some sign he should explore how much he could avail with God. But no one ought to tempt God, when he has from human reason what he may do. [0085C] Whence though he could do all things, he yet says to his own: *If they persecute you in this city, flee into another.* [var: Vulg. Mt 10:23 *Cum autem persequentur vos in civitate ista, fugite in aliam*] And he himself likewise fled and departed and hid himself. Now he could have come down from the temple otherwise than by casting himself down out of boastfulness. When human reason fails, let a man commend himself to God, not by tempting, but by devoutly confessing.

*For he hath given his angels charge over thee. [n: (BEDA.)]* What is rightly said of the body, the devil wrongly interprets of the head, etc., *as far as* but he speaks of the help of the angels as though to a weak man, and is silent about his own being trodden underfoot.

VERS. 8.-- *Again he took him.* This temptation went before in order, but is related out of its place, according to what [0085D] was done in Adam's case.

*He showed him,* etc. Not that he enlarged the sight of him who sees all things, but the vanity of worldly pomp, which he loved, as though it were beautiful, etc., *as far as* Not that he beheld it with the eye of concupiscence as we do, but this showing was in the mind, as physicians see diseases without being harmed by them.

VERS. 9.-- *All these will I give thee.* This he says out of arrogance: not that the whole world is his.

From the beginning the devil labored to usurp for himself what was God's: whence, that he might be worshipped in them, he invented idols. In these three are marked gluttony, avarice, pride.

[n: (RAB.)] Luke sets avarice in the middle, and pride last, [0086A] etc., *as far as* in these three all the kinds of temptations are comprehended.

VERS. 10.-- *It is written.* David laid Goliath low with three stones from the torrent, and Christ laid the devil low with three testimonies from the law. *The Lord thy God.* This is either said to the devil: not because he was going to fulfil it out of devotion, but that, on the contrary to what he himself was attempting, it might be shown by what is written that not he, but God is to be adored: or he hints that this precept was given not to the devil, but to himself according to his humanity, and to any man whatsoever. Likewise also that other word: *Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God,* namely the Son and the Father and the Holy Spirit, who is one God. God is adored, and is served especially for his own sake.

Here it is shown that the man Christ, as God and [0086B] Lord, is to be adored by debt.

*Thou shalt serve.* In Greek λατρεύσεις : for λατρεία is called service. Service common to God and to man and to whomsoever is called in Greek δουλεία. But that which is owed to God alone is called latria: whence idolatry, which gives to idols what it owes to God alone.

Note that the devil is conquered in those things in which he conquered Adam. Him he tempted by gluttony, when he asked him to taste of the forbidden tree. By vainglory, when he said [n: (Gen. III)]: *You shall be as gods.* By avarice, when he said: *Knowing good and evil.*

VERS. 11.-- *They came.* Not as though then coming to him for the first time, but beholding the Lord's contest from afar, lest he should seem to have needed their protection or to have conquered by it. But when the other went away conquered, they came ready for his service. As [0086C] in this contest our warfare is laid out beforehand, so in the service of the angels a glorious recompense is taught.

VERS. 12.-- *And when he had heard. [n: (RAB.)]* Here Matthew, like Mark and Luke, passes over the Lord's first coming into Galilee, after which, etc., *as far as, This beginning of miracles did Jesus.* And again: *John was not yet cast into prison.* [var: Vulg. Jo 3:24 *Nondum enim missus fuerat Joannes in carcerem*]

*John,* etc. Which was for the Gospel's sake. Jesus, preaching this same thing more perfectly, gives place for a time and flees, that he may be an example to his own. *Into Galilee.* There are two Galilees: one is called the Galilee of the Jews, the other of the Gentiles, because of the dwelling of Gentiles there, which portion Solomon gave to the king of Tyre, who settled Gentiles there.

[0086D]VERS. 13.-- *Nazareth. [n: (RAB.)]* From which Christ is called a Nazarene, is a village in Galilee beside mount Thabor, etc., *as far as* because in the midst of the Gentiles it stands firm for the spreading abroad of the word of God, that it may show to believers in peril the harbor of faith.

VERS. 15.-- *The land of Zabulon. [n: (ID.)]* The evangelist passes over what stands first; namely: *In the first time the land of Zabulon and the land of Nephtalim was lightened [n: (Isa. IX)]*: as also what stands in the middle, etc., *as far as* but for a figure of those who are to be called from among the Gentiles, that which is of the Gentiles is here mentioned.

VERS. 16.-- *The people. [n: (AUG.)]* That people which was first led into captivity, and was in the darkness of vices, first saw the light of Christ's preaching. Thereafter [0087A] the Gospel was scattered abroad among all. Whence it follows: *To them that dwell in the region.* [var: Vulg. Mt 4:16 *sedentibus in regione*, "to them that sit"]

*Of the shadow of death.* Death is in hell. The shadow of this death are sins, which are never without death. He therefore who wishes to flee death, let him avoid the shadow.

VERS. 17.-- *From that time.* After he was baptized. Baptism makes men fit for preaching. *From that time,* that is, John having been delivered up: because when the law ceases the Gospel follows, as the sun follows the dawn. A humble master, who does not hinder the teaching of his disciple, but waits until he complete his course. In which he teaches that no one should despise a word from a lesser person. Whence the Apostle. *If anything be revealed to another, let the first hold his peace.* [var: Vulg. 1Cor 14:30 *Quod si alii revelatum fuerit sedenti, prior taceat*]
