And when it has been leavened into one, it leads us not to a threefold God, but to the knowledge of one deity, because the nature is not diverse in the several persons.

*Until it was leavened.* So long ought charity, hidden in the mind, to grow, until it change the whole mind into its own perfection, so that it love or think upon nothing beside God, which is begun here, and perfected in the other life.

VERS. 34.-- *In parables to the crowds.* Because whatsoever [0133C] is there said of the army of Israel, and all the signs, are hidden sacraments.

VERS. 44.-- *To a treasure hidden in a field.* By the treasure may be understood the word of God, which is hidden in the flesh of Christ. Or the Scripture, in which the knowledge of the Saviour is laid up. Or the two Testaments in the Church, for the understanding of which all things are renounced, that they may be learned in leisure.

The kingdom of heaven is likened to earthly things, that through things known the mind may rise to things unknown, and love them.

*He hideth it, and for joy thereof.* That it may be kept safe from malignant spirits and from the praises of men. Let the work be so in public, that the intention remain hidden.



## CHAPTER XIII. (cont.)

VERS. 45.-- *To a merchant.* The blessedness of which we were stripped by the fault of the first man, we ought all to trade with, by understanding [0133D] rightly and working well. *Good pearls.* The good pearls are the law and the prophets. The one precious pearl is the knowledge of the Saviour, for which a man, like Paul, renounced all the mysteries and observances of the law.

VERS. 46.-- *But having found.* That is, Christ, who is over all men, or the spiritual precept of love. Or the Word understood, which was with God, the shell of the flesh being pierced through. Or the sweetness of the heavenly life, in comparison with which all things grow cheap.

VERS. 47.-- *To a net cast.* The prophecy of Jeremias is fulfilled: *Behold I send to you many fishers [n: (Jer. XVI)]* [var: Vulg. Jr 16:16 *Ecce ego mittam piscatores multos*, "Behold I will send many fishers"; the verb is future, and there is no "to you"]. After Peter and Andrew, James and John had heard: *Follow me, I will make you fishers of men:* [var: Vulg. Mt 4:19 *Venite post me, et faciam vos fieri piscatores hominum*, "Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men"] they wove themselves a net out of the Old [0134A] and the New Testament, and cast it into the sea of the world; which is drawn even to this day, and is stretched among the waves: taking whatsoever falls in, good and bad, whom it draws to the shore, that is, to the end of the world, that then the division may be made. Whence follows: *So shall it be at the consummation of the world,* etc. To a net is compared the Church, or the preaching of the Gospel, which draws from the waves of the world to heaven.

VERS. 48.-- *And by the shore.* The shore is the end of the world, in which the good shall be sent to heaven, the bad to darkness: for in the present they were mingled together.

VERS. 52.-- *Therefore every Scribe instructed,* etc. Because you understand the mysteries which I reveal to you: therefore I will make you preachers, and you shall be like me, who out of the treasure of my knowledge bring forth new things and old, that you [0134B] may do likewise.

The apostles are the scribes and notaries of Christ, marking his words upon the tablets of the heart, and they are strong in the riches of a householder, bringing forth out of the treasure of their doctrines new things and old, because whatsoever is preached in the Gospel they confirm by the voices of the law and of the prophets.

VERS. 54.-- *So that they wondered.* A great blindness, him whom by words and deeds they recognize to be Christ, they despise on account of their acquaintance with his family.

VERS. 55.-- *The carpenter's son.* Not without cause did he will to be called the carpenter's son, not of him whom they suppose, but of the maker of all things. But the Jews, ignorant of this sacrament, despise the works of the divine power by looking upon his fleshly lineage. For they do not consider his present works, but remember his frail infancy.

[0134C]VERS. 57.-- *A prophet.* Christ is called a prophet. Whence Moses says: *The Lord shall raise up to you a prophet out of your seed [n: (Deut. XVIII)]* [var: Vulg. Dt 18:15 *Prophetam de gente tua et de fratribus tuis, sicut me, suscitabit tibi Dominus Deus tuus*, "A prophet of thy nation and of thy brethren, like unto me, shall the Lord thy God raise up unto thee"]. *In his own country.* That is, among the people of the Jews: but he does greater things among the Gentiles.

VERS. 58.-- *And he did not.* He did some miracles, but not many, lest he should condemn the unbelieving. Or, being despised, he does few, lest they be wholly excusable, but he does greater things among the Gentiles.



## CHAPTER XIV.

VERS. 1.-- *At that time Herod heard.* But Luke thus: *And Herod the tetrarch heard [n: (Luc. IX)]*, etc. What therefore he says: *This is John [n: (Joan. IV)]*. Either he said it after his hesitation, being confirmed by the opinion of certain men, or being still in doubt: for these words admit of either.

[0134D]VERS. 2.-- *And he said.* Mark the envy of the Jews. Here a foreigner says that John has risen again, who wrought no sign. They contend that Jesus, approved by so many miracles, has not risen again. *And therefore.* For they perceived that the saints, rising again from the dead, are to be of greater power than when weighed down with frail flesh.

VERS. 3.-- *For Herod.* Because he spoke of the opinion of the resurrection when he had said nothing of the death, he turns back and relates how and why he died. This Herod and Philip were brothers, sons of that Herod under whom the Lord fled into Egypt. *Herodias his brother's wife.* Herodias was the daughter of king Aretas, whom her own father took away from Philip, and, to Philip's grief, gave to Herod his enemy.

VERS. 4.-- *It is not lawful.* Herod perhaps held the law of the Jews [0135A], and therefore John forbade him the adultery.

VERS. 5.-- *He feared the people.* He feared the people, but love prevailed, for which he even set God behind. The fear of God corrects; the fear of men puts off, but does not take away the will: whence it also makes the more eager for the crime those whom for a time it holds back from the crime.

VERS. 7.-- *With an oath.* Perhaps he swore to this end, that he might prepare an occasion by which he should seem to do unwillingly what he was doing of his own accord. For he would not have fulfilled this concerning anyone he loved, which he fulfilled concerning the prophet: which he would have done even before, if he could have done it excusably.

[n: (BEDA.)] If it should happen that we have perhaps sworn something incautiously, etc., *as far as* nor did he grieve that he had contracted any fault to himself by such perjury.

[0135B] [n: (ISID.)] An oath is not to be kept whereby an evil is incautiously promised, as if, etc., *as far as* for it is more tolerable not to fulfil an oath than to remain in defilement.

VERS. 9.-- *Being made sorrowful [sic: Constristatus].* As it seemed to those that sat at meat. For such was the sorrow of Herod as was, namely, the repentance of Pharaoh.

VERS. 10.-- *And he beheaded.* John was made less by the head, Christ was lifted up on the cross: because the fame of the one decreased, that of the other increased; whence: *He must increase, but I must decrease [n: (Joan. III)]*. In the severed head of John it is shown that the Jews had lost Christ (who is the head of all the prophets).

Morally. The death of John signifies the end of the law, which being ended, one deservedly passes over to Christ, who is the end [0135C] of the law unto justice to everyone that believeth.

VERS. 13.-- *And when Jesus had heard it.* After among the Jews the law and the prophet lose their head and their voice: Jesus passes over to the desert place of the Church, which before had no husband. *He withdrew.* He did not flee out of fear, but he withdrew, sparing his enemies, lest they should join murder to murder, giving an example of rashness to be shunned. Or *he withdrew,* that he might prove the faith of them that believe; whence: *And when the crowds had heard,* etc. *On foot.* By their own labour, that they might show the ardour of their mind. They leave the cities, that is, their former ways of life. They have the will, but not the strength to arrive. Therefore Jesus goes out to meet them, and having pity heals them, that a full faith may have its reward at once. Behold how greatly he is delighted with the devotion of them that believe.

VERS. 15.-- *And when it was evening,* etc. Jesus withdraws [0135D] from Judea, goes into the desert, the crowds follow, whom he meets and heals. This not in the morning or at midday, but in the evening, when the sun of justice had set and the end of the world had drawn near.

*His disciples.* Carnal, and ignorant of the coming miracle of the refreshment, to whom it had been said: *Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles [n: (Matth. X)]*.

Mystically. The Jews disdain that the Gentiles should be received, and they murmur: whose voice Isaias uses [n: (Isa. XL)]: *Behold the nations are as a drop of a bucket.* Again: *All nations are as though they were not, but they are before him.* [var: Vulg. Is 40:17 *sic sunt coram eo*, "so are they before him"] But the Lord determined to refresh them by the apostles; whence he subjoins: *But Jesus,* etc.

*Send away the crowds.* It is long that she has followed idols, and therefore she is not to be fed by us with the bread of the word of God.

[0136A]VERS. 16.-- *Give ye them.* He provokes them to give, that, when they testify that they have nothing, the greatness of the sign may be the better known; wherein he also hints that by them the hungry hearts are to be fed.

VERS. 17.-- *Five loaves and two fishes.* By the five loaves and the two fishes the whole Old Testament is signified. By the five loaves, the five books of Moses, which are well of barley, which is the food of beasts of burden, for to the untaught things rough and coarse must be given. *For the sensual man perceiveth not the things that are of the spirit of God [n: (I Cor. I)]* [var: Vulg. 1 Cor 2:14 *Animalis autem homo*, "But the sensual man"]. Within, nevertheless, lies hidden the marrow of a most sweet meaning. By the two fishes, the prophets and the psalms: whence also after the resurrection he says: *The things that are written in the law and in very many prophets concerning me [n: (Luc. XXIV)]* [var: Vulg. Lc 24:44 *in lege Moysi, et prophetis, et Psalmis de me*, "in the law of Moses, and the prophets, and the psalms concerning me"; the gloss's own point is the psalms].

VERS. 19.-- *Having taken the five,* etc. He took five [0136B] loaves, he did not create new ones, because coming in the flesh he preached no other things than those which had been foretold, and fulfilled them in deed. *He blessed.* When, opening their understanding that they might understand the Scriptures, he multiplied them by the gift of an inward sweetness. He broke, when he brought forth the mysteries of the law into the midst.

VERS. 20.-- *The fragments.* The more secret things, which cannot be grasped by the untaught, are not to be held negligently, but are to be diligently sought out by the twelve apostles, who are signified by the twelve baskets, and by their successors. With baskets servile works are carried on. *And the weak things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the strong [n: (I Cor. I)]*.

VERS. 21.-- *Besides women and children.* The frail sex and the lesser age are unworthy of the number. It signifies those weak in faith, not yet fit for battle.

VERS. 22. *And immediately he compelled,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Who, [0136C] as John says, *were about to come to make him king [n: (Joan. VI)]*, who had seen the miracle of the loaves, etc., *as far as* let us pray for them, lest they soften us.

VERS. 23.-- *He went up.* He fed the crowd as God, he went up to pray as man. Not as one not having all things in his power, but that he might fulfil the form of a man. In this there is a duty of piety; there follows a notable miracle of power. *And when it was evening.* Rightly is this storm said to be in the evening, because while the Church is in tribulation, she is said to be as it were in the night, and the sun of justice seems to have hidden himself.

VERS. 24.-- *But the boat.* The ship in the midst of the sea, Jesus alone on the land: because sometimes the Church is so, not only afflicted but also defiled, that she seems utterly forsaken by God: but God does not [0136D] forsake her. Whence Mark says: *He saw them labouring in rowing [n: (Marc. VI)]* [var: Vulg. Mc 6:48 *videns eos laborantes in remigando*, "seeing them labouring in rowing"]. Though not present, and though he defers, yet he sees and strengthens.

VERS. 25.-- *And in the fourth.* [var: Vulg. Mt 14:25 *Quarta enim vigilia noctis*, "For in the fourth watch of the night"] They are in peril the whole night, because when a man considers himself, he finds nothing but the darkness of straits and the surgings of enemies.

*He came to them.* Mark says: *Willing to pass by them,* for whose deliverance nevertheless he came. Which happens so that, being troubled for an hour but soon delivered, they may wonder the more, and give thanks; which same thing often happens in the passions of the saints.

VERS. 26.-- *And seeing him,* etc. Because it often happens that when some sudden abatement of a long tribulation arises, it is not straightway believed to be a true deliverance. And therefore, the former dread remaining intense [0137A], prayer is directed toward deliverance.

VERS. 27.-- *It is I, fear ye not.* He does not add who, because from the voice known to them they could recognize him. Or because he himself is he who said: *He who is hath sent me to you [n: (Exod. III)]*.

VERS. 28.-- *Lord, if it be thou.* If thou art that deliverer, bid me come to the imitation of thee by overcoming pressures.

VERS. 29.-- *And going down.* Despairing of human help, he treads down pressures with his mind, that he may be conformed to Jesus. *He walked,* etc. Behold, a man walks upon the waters. Doubt not therefore that Christ is a true body, because he walked upon the waters.

He made him walk upon the sea, that he might show the divine [0137B] power. He makes him sink, lest he forget his infirmity, lest he think himself equal to God, and lest he grow proud.

VERS. 30.-- *And when he had begun,* etc. He is left a little to temptation, that faith may be increased; for as he believed that by his command he could be upheld upon the waves, so, while he sinks, that he could be saved by his power.

VERS. 32.-- *The wind ceased.* In whomsoever God is present by grace, straightway all wars grow quiet.

VERS. 33.-- *And they adored him,* etc. The sign being seen, they confess him the Son of God: why then should Arius bring it about that he is a creature?

VERS. 34.-- *Into the land of Genesar.* Allegorically. Genesar is interpreted *the garden of princes.* By the type therefore of the apostles and of the ship, it is to be understood that the Church, delivered from persecutions, is led by the Lord [0137C] to the shore, that is, to rest, where the inheritance of paradise and the gladness of the first robe shall be restored.

VERS. 36.-- *The hem of his garment,* etc. That is, the least commandment, or the flesh by which we come to the word of God, and he who touches him by believing is healed of every disease of impiety.



## CHAPTER XV.

VERS. 1.-- *Then they drew near.* The men of Genesar, being less learned, believe, but those who seem wise come for a fight.

[n: (CHRYSOST.)] Then, he says, that is, when he had wrought countless signs, when, etc., *as far as* that he might show how great their malice was.

VERS. 2.-- *For they wash not.* Within they reprove nothing, [0137D] who within are polluted with spite. In vain indeed do they keep their washings, who neglect to wash away the filth of their own hearts and bodies.

VERS. 3.-- *Why do you also transgress.* If you despise the commandments of God for the sake of the traditions of men, why do you reprove the disciples, who let go the commandments of men that they may keep the decrees of God?

VERS. 4.-- *Honour father. [n: (HIER.)]* Honour, in the Scriptures, is not so much in salutations and in the paying of courtesies, as, etc., *as far as* that sons should honour their parents also in the ministering of the necessaries of life.

VERS. 5.-- *But you say,* etc. But your tradition is contrary. You compel sons to say this to their parents: [0138A] What I was to have offered to God I spend upon food for thee, and it profits thee, O father, that he should be afraid to eat what has been consecrated. Or: what I offer to God profits thee thyself. *Whosoever shall say.* That is, he will be worthy of eternal life. Or *shall say,* that is, to say it will profit. *It shall profit.* As if he said: No, nay, thou wouldst be sacrilegious if thou didst take it, because I have vowed it to God, *Or it shall profit thee:* if I shall have given it to God.

VERS. 7.-- *Well hath he prophesied,* etc. In the spirit, the dissembling of the Jews, that in guile they would fight against the Gospel.

VERS. 8.-- *He honoureth me with the lips. Master, we know that thou art true [n: (Marc. XII)]*. Or, by commending outward cleanness — the inward, and that which is true, is not in them.

[0138B]VERS. 11.-- *Not that which entereth in.* There is nothing outside a man that defiles him within, nor meat offered to idols in this, that it is God's creature; by one word every superstition of observances is struck down, when religion is thought to lie in distinguishing foods.

VERS. 12.-- *Then the disciples, drawing near.* Great is the Pharisees' religion in the matter of foods, who on hearing this word were scandalized, that is, were indignant. *They were scandalized.* Σκάνδαλον in Greek, we can say a stumbling-block, or a ruin, or the striking of the foot. Whence: He that shall scandalize anyone, that is, shall have given occasion of ruin.

VERS. 14.-- *Let them alone,* etc. Leave them to their own judgment, because they are past recall. Whence Paul: *A man that is a heretic, after the first and second correction, avoid* [0138C] [n: (Tit. III)]. [var: Vulg. Tit 3:10 *post unam et secundam correptionem*, "after one and a second rebuke"]

VERS. 15.-- *Expound.* What was said plainly, the apostles think was said in a parable. He is a faulty hearer who wishes to understand either obscure things plainly, or things plainly said obscurely.

VERS. 19.-- *Out of the heart,* etc. For they are not sent in by the devil, but are born of a man's own will. For the devil is an inciter, not an author, since neither does he know inward things save through outward bearing and gesture.

VERS. 20.-- *With unwashen hands.* The spiritual sayings of the prophets, concerning the chastening of the heart and of the body, such as these: *Be washed, be clean [n: (Isa. I)]*. The Pharisees took them carnally, of the body alone, which it is vain to do.

VERS. 21.-- *And going out,* etc. The slanderers being left behind, [0138D] within the borders of Tyre and Sidon, that he might set the daughter free, and by the faith of a Gentile woman convict the perfidy of the Scribes. "The slanderers being left behind" signifies that after the resurrection he would leave behind the perfidy of the Jews, and would go by his preaching to the Gentiles.

VERS. 22.-- *She cried out,* etc. By faith she cries out, whence, she knows how to call him Son of David, confessing the incarnation of Christ. She prays for her daughter, that is, for her own people not yet believing, that they may be loosed from that very deceit of the devil. Or, the daughter is the soul or the conscience of anyone within the Church that has been made over to the devil, for which mother Church prays, or the man himself for his defiled conscience.

VERS. 23.-- *Who answered not.* Not out of pride, but lest he should be contrary to his own saying: *Into the way of the Gentiles [0139A] go ye not [n: (Matth. X)]*. Whence he avoids the slander of the Jews, but the salvation of the Gentiles is reserved for the time of the passion and the resurrection.

VERS. 24.-- *I was not sent.* As if he said: First I must fulfil the sacrament of my coming among the Jews, and so bring in other sheep, and this by deferring, in the matter of the sign, the petition of this woman.

VERS. 26.-- *The children's bread.* The word of salvation, which is owed first to the Jews, is not good to give to dogs, or to the Gentiles, that always bark with a dog's madness.

VERS. 27.-- *Yea, Lord.* Under the person of the woman, the marvellous faith of the Church, and her patience, and her humility are proclaimed. Faith, because she believes that her daughter can be healed. Patience, because so often despised she persists in her prayers. [0139B] Humility, because she compares herself not to dogs, but to whelps.

*For even the whelps.* The table is Holy Scripture; the children's crumbs are the inward mysteries with which the humble are refreshed under the table: because, being humbly subject to the Scriptures, the whelps are the humble Gentiles. The little ones eat not loaves, not crusts, that is, not the surface of the letter, but the marrow.

VERS. 28.-- *Great is the faith.* So above, of the centurion: *I have not found so great faith in Israel [n: (Matth. VIII)]*, who likewise (as this Canaanite woman does) prefigured the faith of the Gentiles. Great is the faith of the Gentiles, who at the hearing of the ear obey: and in God she obtains salvation for herself and for her own. That he heals the centurion's servant and the Canaanite woman's daughter without coming to them signifies that the Gentiles, [0139C] to whom he did not come by his presence, were to be saved by his word.

*And she was healed.* Here an example is given of catechizing and baptizing infants, who can neither understand nor do anything, but are set free from the devil through the faith and confession of their parents.

VERS. 29.-- *And when he had passed over.* When in the daughter of the Canaanite woman he had prefigured the salvation of the Gentiles, he returns into Judaea, because when the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in, then all Israel shall be saved. *Into a mountain.* The Lord on the mountain, the Word, sits on high: because in his own majesty he could not be understood.

VERS. 30.-- *The blind.* The blind are those who do not understand, even if they obey those who command. The deaf, those who do not obey, even if they understand.

[0139D]VERS. 32.-- *But Jesus.* He calls the disciples together, that he may teach masters to share their counsels with their inferiors. Or that from his speech they may understand the greatness of the sign. *I have compassion on the crowd.* The crowd endures with the Lord for three days, because faithful penitents turn themselves to the Lord in deed and in word and in thought, who would faint on the way of the present life if they were left in their own conscience without the food of doctrine. In the earlier sign the kinsfolk are called to mind, and the neighbours of the five senses, and the Lord does not remember them, but the disciples do, at evening, the sun being now declined. Here the Lord says that he has compassion, and why: because they have now continued with me three days. In the whole world the third is the time in which grace is given: the first before the law, the second under the law, [0140A] the third under grace, the fourth is in the world to come, where there will be day without night, toward which, as he presses on, a man is refreshed on the way.

VERS. 33.-- *Loaves in the desert.* The loaves are the preachers, the desert, themselves, that is, they call themselves unfruitful. As if he said: Whence have we such eloquence that we can suffice for hearers so greedy?

VERS. 36.-- *And taking.* That he may show that he rejoices together with us over the salvation of men, and he forms us to give thanks even for temporal things. *Seven loaves.* He feeds with the sevenfold Spirit, with apostolic authority joined to it, as with the savour of a few fishes, who refresh us by the example of their life or of their death. Seven loaves: the Scripture of the New Testament, in which the grace of the Holy Spirit is both revealed and given. Nor are they of barley, [0140B] as above, because here the life-giving food of the soul is not (as in the law) covered over with figures, like a most clinging husk. Here there are not two fishes (as in the law two were anointed, the king and the priest), but a few, that is, the saints of the New Testament, who have been snatched from the waves of the world, and endure the troubled sea, and refresh us by their example, lest we faint on the way.

[n: (BEDA.)] There upon the grass, that the desires of the flesh may be pressed down, here upon the ground, where the world itself also, etc., *as far as* both refreshments were celebrated on a mountain, because the Scripture of both Testaments enjoins the height of the heavenly precepts and of the rewards: both proclaim the height of Christ.

*And that which was left over.* The higher mysteries which the common crowd does not grasp, the apostles take up and fill [0140C] seven baskets, that is, the hearts of the perfect, enlightened for understanding by the sevenfold grace of the Spirit. *Seven baskets.* Baskets are wont to be woven of rush and of palm leaves, and they signify the saints, who set the root of the heart in the very fountain of life, lest they wither, as the rush in the water: and they keep the palm of the eternal reward in their heart.

VERS. 39.-- *And having sent away the crowd.* Here he teaches that preachers, when the word has been ministered to the crowd, ought themselves to be refreshed within the chamber of the heart with the fruits of the virtues. *Into the coasts.* Magedan, which by another name is called Dalmanutha, which is the region about Gerasa. And it is interpreted *fruits* or tidings, and it signifies the garden of which it is said: *A garden enclosed, a fountain sealed,* where the fruits of the virtues grow. And there the name of the Lord is announced.



## CHAPTER XVI.

[0140D]

VERS. 1.-- *And they came,* etc. *That he would show a sign from heaven,* etc. That he who fed many with few things should rain down manna wherewith to refresh all. Whence John, after the eating of the loaves: *What sign dost thou do, that we may see and believe thee? what dost thou work? Our fathers did eat manna in the desert [n: (Joan. VI)]*. They asked by way of tempting, that after the manner of Elias he should send fire from on high, or in the likeness of Samuel should make the thunders roar in the summer season, as though they could not have slandered those things too, and said that they had come to pass from the hidden and various affections of the air.

VERS. 2.-- *When it is evening.* He rebukes them, because from the order of the elements they distinguish the days, but the signs of the times [0141A] they do not know, since the whole law and the prophets signify the tokens of his coming out of the wonder of the works that he was to do.

VERS. 3.-- *For it is red.* The apostles suffer after the resurrection, by whom you can know that I shall judge in time to come, because when I do not spare my own good ones but that they suffer, I shall not spare others in time to come.

VERS. 4.-- *Signs.* Things belonging to the time of grace, foretold by the prophets, cannot make you believe concerning my coming. *But the signs.* He spoke of the signs of the times concerning his own coming or his passion, to which a rosy sky at evening is like. And likewise concerning the tribulation before the coming that is to be, to which a rosy sky with gloom is like. *It shall not be given him.* But it is given to the faithful from heaven, when, the apostles looking on, he ascended into heaven, [0141B] and sent the Holy Spirit.

VERS. 5.-- *They forgot to take bread.* How do they not have loaves, who but now, the baskets being filled, went up into the boat, and as they sail hear that they are to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. But nevertheless the Scripture says that they forgot to take loaves with them, being caught by the sweetness of the one true and inward bread (who was with them), judging that they cared little about the care of the body and about necessaries, since even natural refreshment itself had passed from their mind.

VERS. 6.-- *Of the leaven.* Leaven is perverse doctrine, which even in small quantity corrupts the whole mass, and draws it into its own savour.

VERS. 8.-- *Why do you think.* Why do you think that I spoke of earthly loaves, about which you need not be in doubt, since out of so few I made so many [0141C] leavings abound?

VERS. 11.-- *Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.* Of superstitious doctrine, which after the manner of leaven feigns that it has the substance of true bread. By this he hints what the five loaves or the seven signify. For if by leaven he means heretical teachings, the loaves are true doctrine.

VERS. 13.-- *Into the parts of Caesarea Philippi.* This is the place where the Jordan rises at the foot of Lebanon, out of Jor and Dan, two springs. *That men say he is.* They are men who speak of the Son of man: for they are gods who understand the Godhead. *The Son of man?* The Lord professes of himself the lowliness of his humanity, while the disciples understand his Godhead.

VERS. 14.-- *Some, John the Baptist.* So they could [0141D] err about Elias or about the rest of the others, as Herod erred about John when he said: *John, whom I beheaded, is risen from the dead: and therefore mighty works are wrought in him [n: (Marc. VI)]* [var: Vulg. Mc 6:16 *Quem ego decollavi Joannem, hic a mortuis resurrexit*, "John, whom I beheaded, he is risen again from the dead", and the clause about the mighty works belongs to Mc 6:14, *et propterea virtutes operantur in illo*]. Therefore he wills that their errors be set forth, so that, these being driven off, the disciples may bring forth the truth, not out of the opinion of the common people, but out of the Lord's revelation.

VERS. 17.-- *Simon Peter answering.* Therefore one answers, and to one answer is made on behalf of all, that unity may be kept in all. *Of the living God.* For a distinction from the false gods, which the Gentiles set up for themselves either out of dead men or out of sensible matter.

*Barjona.* Well is he the son of the dove, because he followed the Lord with a devout simplicity, or because he was full of spiritual grace. He is called the son of the Holy Spirit, [0142A] who was shown in the dove, by him whom he had called the Son of the living God, and to the son of the dove the Father reveals, because the operation of the Father and of the Son with the Holy Spirit is one. He reveals, I say, the mystery of faith, because flesh and blood could not reveal it, that is, men puffed up with carnal wisdom, who are not sons of the dove, and therefore strangers to the wisdom of the Spirit; of whom above: *Others John the Baptist, and others Elias,* etc.

VERS. 18.-- *Thou art.* I do not say, thou shalt be called, but thou art Peter, for the strength of thy faith and the constancy of thy confession. *Peter.* From me, the Rock, yet so that I keep for myself the dignity of the foundation: thou shalt set clean stones upon me, and shalt cast away the leprous.

Just as light and the other names, as: *You are the salt of the earth,* were allotted to the apostles by the Lord, so to Simon he gave from [0142B] himself the name of Peter.

*And the gates.* The gates of hell are sins, threats, blandishments, heresies, by which the weak rush into death, who are to be believed to have built the house of their profession not truly upon the rock, but upon the sand, that is, not to follow Christ with a simple and true intention, but to have put forward the habit for some earthly cause. For he who receives the faith of Christ in the inmost love of the heart easily overcomes whatever assails him from without.

VERS. 19.-- *And whatsoever thou shalt bind.* That is, whomsoever thou shalt have adjudged to eternal punishments as persisting in his sins, or whomsoever thou shalt have absolved as humble and truly penitent, so shall it be also in heaven.

*And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth. [n: (HIER.)]* The other apostles have [0142C] indeed the same judicial power, to whom after the resurrection he says: *Receive ye the Holy Spirit [n: (Joan. XX)]*, etc., *as far as* whence in Leviticus the lepers are bidden to show themselves to the priests, whom the priests do not make lepers, but discern who are clean or unclean, so also here.

VERS. 20.-- *That they should tell no man,* etc. Above he commands them to preach his coming, here that they should not say that he is Jesus. But it is one thing to preach Christ, which is a common name of dignity: another to preach Jesus, which is the Saviour's own name. As if he said: It does not profit that my majesty be publicly preached to the peoples, who are to see me suffer many things, which will be lawful only then, when the resurrection shall have shown the power of the Godhead. *Jesus Christ.* The Saviour: lest they should be scandalized in him whom a little [0142D] after they are to see spat upon and crucified.

VERS. 21.-- *From that time,* etc. Behold the reason why the preaching was forbidden, as if he said: Preach me then, when I shall have suffered these things, because before that it does not profit.

VERS. 22.-- *Far be it.* Peter does not wish his own confession to be destroyed, nor does he think that the Son of God can be slain.

VERS. 23.-- *Go.* Above: all those glorious things were promised for the future, not given in the present. *I will build my Church, and to thee I will give the keys,* etc. Which if he had given at once, error would never afterwards have found place in him. *Because thou savourest not.* It does not please thee that I should redeem the world by my death, which is the will of the Father: but thou savourest these things carnally.

[0143A]VERS. 24.-- *If any man will.* The passion and the resurrection having been foretold to the apostles, he exhorts both them and the crowds to follow. *Let him deny himself.* That which is by oldness, that he may take hold of that which is beyond himself. Vices being removed, let virtue follow: let him take up his cross, and follow me. That which was by oldness, he had denied who said: *But I myself live, now not I.* [var: Vulg. Gal 2:20 *Vivo autem, jam non ego*, without the emphatic *ego* Migne adds after *Vivo autem*] But that which was beyond himself he had begun: *yet Christ liveth in me [n: (Gal. II)]*. *Let him take up his cross.* That is: the cross is taken up either when the body is afflicted through abstinence, or when the mind is afflicted through compassion for one's neighbour. Paul had the cross of abstinence when he said [n: (II Cor. XI)]: *I chastise my body and bring it into subjection.* And the cross of compassion too, when he says: *Who is weak, and I am not weak?*

[0143B]VERS. 26.-- *For what doth it profit.* The Church has a time of persecution: it has also a time of peace. These times he designates in his precepts. For in the time of persecution the soul must be laid down, and in the time of peace earthly desires must be broken.

*Or what,* etc. Let neither gains, nor fear, nor anything else draw a man back from salvation: because *what exchange shall a man give,* etc. *I will take the chalice of salvation, and I will call upon the name of the Lord [n: (Psal. CXV)]*. Or: a man will be able to give nothing earthly for a soul that is lost.

VERS. 27.-- *For the Son.* Nor let it seem hard to suffer this: *Because the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come, that shall be revealed in us [n: (Rom. VIII)]*.

VERS. 28.-- *There are some.* Because the apostles were untaught, there is promised them even in the present life some [0143C] consolation, that they may believe the more surely concerning the life to come. *In the kingdom.* In the kingdom of eternal blessedness, or by showing his power in the Church that now is.



## CHAPTER XVII.

VERS. 1.-- *And after days,* etc. Mark says the same, but Luke eight. These therefore set down the middle days, Luke adds, etc., *as far as* and in the world to come they shall be parted in every way, when he shall hide them in the hiding of his face from the disturbance of men.

*Peter.* The names of these men are fitting. Each ought to be Peter, that is, firm in faith. Then James, that is, the supplanter of vices. Then John, that is, one ascribing all things to divine grace against the pride [0143D] of life, which is wont to arise out of the virtues.

VERS. 2.-- *He was transfigured.* The form which he had by nature he showed, not losing the flesh which he had assumed by will. But that body which he had by nature he gave to his disciples at the supper, not mortal, not corruptible. *His face did shine.* As a pattern of the blessedness and brightness to come, which the just shall see, the wicked being first taken away. *And his garments,* etc. They were made white, which they were not before, because it hath not yet appeared what we shall be, but when it shall appear, we shall be like to him. Mark says, such as a fuller upon earth cannot make. That is, God cannot in this life make them so bright, because no one is without sin. No cleanser of himself upon earth will do what God does in heaven, [0144A] cleansing his garment from every defilement. The fuller is a teacher of souls, or one who cleanses his own body.

VERS. 3.-- *And behold.* Of what sort they were, or what they spoke, Luke says: *Seen in majesty, and they spoke of his decease which he was to accomplish in Jerusalem [n: (Luc. IX)]*, that is, his passion and resurrection. They signify the oracles, etc., *as far as* that if Peter, seeing the humanity glorified, is affected with so great joy that he would never wish to be parted from the sight of it, what is to be thought of those who have deserved to see the Godhead.

VERS. 5.-- *As he was yet speaking.* That he who sought a tabernacle may learn that in the resurrection they are to be sheltered not by the roof of houses, but by the grace of the Holy Spirit. *Behold a bright cloud,* etc. As when the Lord was baptized, [0144B] so also when he was glorified the mystery of the holy Trinity is shown: because his glory, which in baptism we confess by believing, in the resurrection we shall praise by seeing. The Holy Spirit there in a dove, here in a bright cloud. Because he who now keeps the faith with a simple heart will then contemplate in open vision what he has believed, and will be sheltered by that grace by which he will be enlightened. *And behold a voice,* etc. Because he asked imprudently, he did not deserve an answer from the Lord: but the voice of the Father bears witness concerning the Son, and teaches Peter, and in him the rest, the truth. *This is the Son.* Moses and Elias are servants, and together with us they ought to prepare in their hearts a tabernacle for the Lord. *Hear ye him.* This the Father now enjoins, which Moses, giving testimony to the incarnation, foretold: *He shall raise up a prophet [n: (Deut. XVIII)]*, etc. As if he said: [0144C] This is he whom Moses promised.

VERS. 6.-- *And the disciples hearing fell upon their face.* For they understood, higher than their sense, the one Godhead of both. They feared, either because they knew that they had erred, or because the cloud covered them, or because they heard the voice of the Father.

VERS. 7.-- *Arise,* etc. Fear being driven off, doctrine is given, which while fear remained would not be heard.

VERS. 8.-- *And lifting up their eyes,* etc. The cloud being taken away, they see Jesus, and that Moses and Elias had vanished: because after the shadow of the law and of the prophets departed, which had covered the apostles with its veil, the true light is found in the Gospel. *But only Jesus.* For if Moses and Elias had remained with Jesus, the voice of the Father would seem uncertain, to which of them it had rather given testimony.

[0144D]VERS. 9.-- *Tell it to no man unless,* etc. [var: Vulg. Mt 17:9 *Nemini dixeritis visionem*, "Tell the vision to no man", and Migne prints *nisi* where the received text has *visionem*] Lest the glory of the kingdom to come, being shown beforehand, should be past belief, and lest among the untaught the cross that followed should make a scandal.

VERS. 10.-- *That Elias must,* etc. It is the tradition of the Pharisees, according to Malachi the prophet, that Elias will come before the coming of the Saviour, and will turn back the hearts of the fathers to the sons and of the sons to the fathers, and will restore all things to their ancient state. The apostles therefore judge that this transformation of glory which they had seen is the last, and they say: If thou hast already come in glory, how does thy forerunner not appear, especially because they had seen Elias too depart.

VERS. 13.-- *Then they understood,* etc. From the token [0145A] of his own passion, which he had often spoken of, and of his forerunner's, which they saw fulfilled.

VERS. 14.-- *And when he was come.* The places agree with the things, etc., *as far as* he comforts the weak, teaches, chastens. *For he is a lunatic.* Mark calls him deaf and dumb, etc., *as far as* that through the creature he may defame the creator.

VERS. 15.-- *And I brought him,* etc. He secretly accuses the disciples, whereas often the impossibility of healing comes not from the fault of those who heal, but of those who are to be healed.

VERS. 16.-- *Answering.* Not overcome by weariness does he who is meek break out into words, but as a physician does with a sick man who acts against his own prescriptions.

VERS. 17.-- *And he rebuked.* Because he was angry not with the man, but with the vice: and through one man he convicts the Jews [0145B] of unbelief. Whence he adds: *Bring him hither to me. And the demon went out of him.* Mark says, etc., *as far as* than before, when it possessed him quietly.

VERS. 19.-- *Because of unbelief.* Behold, when we are not heard, it is no impossibility on the part of him who grants, but the fault of him who prays. For on the contrary, if your faith were as fervent as it is troubled, it would grow warm more and more. *As a grain of mustard seed.* He compares perfect faith to a grain of mustard seed, which is lowly in appearance and fervent in the breast: mean to those who see it, and appearing of no strength, but when bruised by pressures it shows what it has within.

VERS. 20.-- *But this kind.* He shows how the insolence of the devil is overcome, that we may know that all the graver things are to be overcome by fastings and prayers, and that the anger [0145C] of God against us can be appeased by this remedy. *But by prayer.* This changeableness of carnal pleasures is not changed, etc., *as far as* whence it is said: *Pray without ceasing [n: (I Thess. V)]*.

VERS. 21.-- *The Son of man.* He always mixes sad things with glad, that when they have come they may be borne less grievously, as things foreseen.

VERS. 22.-- *And they were sorrowful.* This came not from unbelief, but from love: because they cannot bear to hear anything lowly of him.

VERS. 23.-- *And when they were come to Capharnaum.* Through Augustus Caesar Judaea was made tributary, etc., *as far as* whether he pays the tribute, or gainsays Caesar.

VERS. 24.-- *What is thy opinion.* Before Peter [0145D] can suggest it, the Lord asks, lest the disciples be scandalized at the demand of the tribute, since they see that he knows the things that were done in his absence. *The kings of the earth.* Our Lord was, according to the flesh also, a king's son, born of David, and the Word of the Almighty: therefore, as a son of kings, he did not owe tribute, but for the lowliness of the flesh it becomes him to fulfil all justice.

VERS. 25.-- *Then the sons are free,* etc. The sons of a kingdom are free in every kingdom, then much more are the sons of that kingdom free under which all kingdoms are, in any earthly kingdom whatever.



## CHAPTER XVIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Who, thinkest thou,* etc. From the equality of the price [0146A] by which, in the paying of the tribute, he had been reckoned with the Lord, they judged that Peter was set above all the apostles. *In the kingdom of heaven.* Or the kingdom of God is the teaching of the Gospel, which we ought to obey simply and without any drawing back, as a child does not contradict his teachers.

VERS. 2.-- *And calling to him.* According to Mark, Jesus embraces the child, signifying that the humble are worthy of his embrace and of his love. *A little one,* etc. A little one in age, that he might show a likeness. Or he set himself in the midst, who came not to be ministered unto, but to minister. Or *a little one,* that is, he set the Holy Spirit in their hearts, that by humility they might shun pride.

VERS. 4.-- *Whosoever therefore shall humble himself,* etc. The Lord invites [0146B] his disciples, and all others, that what a child has by nature, that is, innocence and humility, this the disciples and all others may have by virtue. *As this little child.* He will be innocent as this little child, who does not persist in anger: Jesus [cj: *Jesus*; read *laesus*, "when hurt"] does not remember: having seen a woman he does not desire her.

VERS. 6.-- *But he that shall scandalize.* Although this is said generally against all, etc., *as far as* we ought to take counsel, it is expedient, etc. *It is expedient.* Because it is much better to undergo a short punishment for a fault than to be kept for eternal torments. *For God will not judge twice for the same thing.*

VERS. 7.-- *Woe to the man.* Because he is not judged according to the profit that comes of it, but according to the outcome that he intends.

[0146C]VERS. 8.-- *And if thy hand.* He taught above that we should not scandalize believers, etc., *as far as* that under the occasion of piety thou shouldst lie open to scandals. *It is good for thee,* etc. It is better to lead a solitary life than for the necessaries of the present life to lose life eternal.

VERS. 10.-- *See that you despise not.* Thus I enjoin upon you the severity of putting away all friendships, etc., *as far as* the salvation of the weak as far as you can. *For their angels.* Why are they not to be despised? because for them angels are daily sent. [n: (HIER.)] Great is the dignity of souls, that each one should have, from the beginning of its birth, an angel deputed to guard it. *They always see,* etc. They enjoy the manifest vision of God, etc., *as far as* they run within him who is everywhere.

VERS. 12.-- *If a man have a hundred,* etc. The Lord [0146D] had a hundred sheep, etc., *as far as* to whom, for perfection, unity is wanting. *Doth he not leave,* etc. [n: (GREG.)] Because *he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant,* etc., *as far as* whereas it is only so much, if the unjust man condemns what he has done amiss.

VERS. 13.-- *He shall rejoice,* etc. [var: Vulg. Mt 18:13 *gaudet super eam magis*, "he rejoiceth for it more": the present, where Migne prints the future *Gaudebit* — the gloss itself reverts to the present *gaudet* in its next words] The Lord rejoices more over our restoration (because he makes us rejoice the more) than over the unchangeableness of the angels. For the power and the humility of God are known to be greater in our restoration than in our creation.

VERS. 15.-- *But if he shall offend against thee,* etc. For if against God, it is not in our judgment. In this order we ought to shun scandals, that we hurt no one: and that we rebuke the sinner [0147A] with a zeal for justice, and open the bowels of mercy to him that repents. *Rebuke him,* etc. He does not bid us forgive the sinner indiscriminately; but him that repents. He sins thus, who seeing his brother sin keeps silent: as does he who does not pardon the penitent. For what he said, "if he repents, forgive," he prefaced by "if he shall have sinned, rebuke." Let pardon be neither hard, nor indulgence slack.

VERS. 17.-- *Tell the Church.* That it may hold him in detestation, etc., *as far as* they are condemned, that a human sentence is confirmed by the divine sentence. *As the heathen.* More detestable is he who acts under the name of a believer, etc., *as far as* through thefts and through perjuries.

VERS. 18.-- *Amen I say,* etc. So far is your sentence confirmed by the divine, whether for receiving the penitent, or for casting off the obstinate.

[0147B]VERS. 20.-- *If two.* Typically. Where the spirit, the soul and the body have agreed, so that there is no war between them, the flesh lusting against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh, whatsoever they ask shall be done. Because if the body wills what the spirit wills, the asking is only for good things. *There am I in me.* [var: Vulg. Mt 18:20 *ibi sum in medio eorum*, "there am I in the midst of them" — the words the gloss goes on to quote, *ut dicat Deum in medio esse eorum*] That is, every discourse calls to concord and to the peace which he so far commends that he says God is in the midst of them, because peace and charity set up their seat in the peaceable, and he affirms that by the merit of unity all things that are to be asked are to be obtained.

VERS. 23.-- *Therefore is likened.* That you may know that one must forgive one's fellow servants, I will show by a likeness, that if that king and lord forgave his servant, much more must a man forgive his fellow servants.

VERS. 25.-- *And his wife.* Him, not only the people, [0147C] but also the prelates and the subjects, together with all their household or substance, he delivered over to foreign nations for the greatness of their offences: that what they would not pay by vow, they might pay by torment. He commanded them to pay the penalties for their covetousness and their works, as for a wife and children.

VERS. 27.-- *And moved with pity.* The merciful Lord not only loosed the Jewish captivity, but also promised that at the coming of Christ he would give pardon of all sins, if they persisted in what they had begun. *He forgave him.* That is, he loosed him from the weight of carnal observances, and forgave the debt, that is, his former transgressions.

VERS. 28.-- *He found one.* The Gentile people he wearied, as though it were his debtor: saying that the grace of Christ was not unto salvation for them, not only by persuasions, but even by torments [0147D] he exacted carnal observances from them.

VERS. 32.-- *Thou wicked servant.* Often have I forgiven thee thy debts, when thou didst ask in thy straits; but being set free thou hadst no compassion, nay rather thou persecutest the prophets and the apostles, and, ungrateful and presuming upon justice, thou despisest the Gentiles, judging them unworthy of thy fellowship in Christ.



## CHAPTER XIX.

VERS. 3.-- *And they came.* As though he might be caught in a dilemma. If he should say: She is to be put away for any cause whatever, and another is to be married, the preacher of chastity acts against himself. If he says she is not to be put away, he acts against the teaching of Moses and of God. Therefore he tempers his answer, setting the natural law and the first sentence of God over against the second, [0148A] which was granted not by the will of God, but by the necessity of those who sin.

VERS. 4.-- *And female.* He does not say females, that there may be one marriage and not many, which was being sought by the putting away of former wives.

VERS. 5.-- *He shall cleave to a wife.* If a wife be evil in her ways, if wanton, or of any such sort whatever, willing or unwilling we must bear with her. For when we were free, we willingly subjected ourselves to servitude. If a bondwoman is put under a free man, or a bondman under a free woman, it is not reckoned a marriage after it has been found out: so also concerning kindred. *And they shall be two in flesh.* The reward of marriage is one flesh out of two: chastity joined to the spirit is made one spirit. It was done by the wholesome counsel of God that a man should embrace a portion of his own body [0148B] in the woman, lest that should be thought different from himself which he knew to have been fashioned out of himself.

VERS. 6.-- *Let not man separate.* Man separates, when out of desire for a second he puts away the first: God separates (who also joins) when by consent, for the worship of God, because the time is short, we so have wives as though not having them.

VERS. 7.-- *Why then did Moses,* etc. [n: (CHRYS.)] Doctrine displeases sinners, etc., *as far as* that the interpretation of the truth be passed over in silence.

VERS. 9.-- *And shall marry another, committeth adultery. And he that shall marry her that is put away.* Because it could happen that someone should bring a false charge against an innocent woman, and for the sake of a second fasten a crime upon his first wife: so he bids him put away the first in such a way that while she lives he may not have a second. And lest a wife [0148C] should do the same to her husband, the same caution is enjoined, that she should not have a second husband. And because an adulteress does not fear reproach, it is said to the husband that if he marries such a one he is under the charge of adultery, the Scripture says: *He that keepeth an adulteress is foolish and wicked [n: (Prov. XVIII)]*.

VERS. 10.-- *It is not expedient.* They saw the heavy burden of wives, that they are wrathful, given to drink and the like, who nevertheless must be borne with, because, when we were free, we subjected ourselves to servitude.

VERS. 12.-- *For there are.* There are three kinds of eunuchs, two carnal: of those who are so born, and of those who have been cut by captivity and by the pleasures of their mistresses. The third is spiritual: those who, though they could be husbands, are continent for Christ's sake. *Who were made so.* Among these are reckoned also those who under the appearance of religion feign [0148D] chastity. *He that can.* It is the voice of one exhorting, not of one commanding, as though each should weigh his own strength, whether he is able to fulfil the precepts of virginity and of chastity.

VERS. 14.-- *Suffer the little children.* If they are to be holy, why do you forbid them to come to the Father? If evil, why do you pronounce sentence before the fault. *Of such.* For as to what sort they now are, that indeed is mine, in that you honour them: as to what sort they are afterwards to be, that is their own, in that you have pity on them. He does not say, of these, but, of such: that they may show that it is not age that reigns, but character: and to those who have a like innocence and simplicity he promises the reward.

VERS. 15.-- *And when he had laid on.* He lays hands upon little ones, when he bestows the help of grace upon the humble.

VERS. 16.-- *And behold one. [n: (BED.)]* He had heard [0149A] that those like a little child are worthy of the kingdom, and he wishes it to be set forth more certainly, not by parables but openly, by what merits he might obtain life. [n: (HIER.)] This young man was both rich and proud. And according to another evangelist he questions him not with the intent of one learning but of one tempting.

VERS. 17.-- *Why askest thou me concerning good?* Because he called him a good master, and did not confess him God, or the Son of God: he says that any holy man whatever is not good in comparison with God. But Christ does not refuse the testimony of goodness, but shuts out the error of a master apart from God. He does not deny that he is a good master, but he says that no master apart from God is good. *Keep the commandments.* This man had asked, what shall I do? in return he does not say, learn: because God, the maker of the rational creature, had taught him: showing [0149B] that he is not good who asks about the good, but he who does what is good.

VERS. 20.-- *The young man saith to him. [n: (BED.)]* [var: Vulg. Mt 19:20 *Dicit illi adolescens*, and Migne prints *ei* where the received text has *illi*] This man is not to be thought (as some say) either to have tempted the Lord, or to have lied about his own life, but he confessed simply as he had lived: otherwise (as another Evangelist says) Jesus, looking into the secrets of his heart, would not be said to love him. For he loves those who keep the commandments of the law, but what is lacking there he adds for those who wish to be perfect; whence there follows: *If thou wilt be perfect. All these. [n: (HIER.)]* He lies. For if he loved his neighbour as himself, he would have fulfilled it in deed, and would not have been sad when he was bidden to give his own goods to the poor.

VERS. 23.-- *A rich man hardly.* Not the rich who remain such, but those who have ceased to be such, shall enter. Of all things it is safer [0149C] neither to have nor to love riches.

VERS. 24.-- *Than for a rich man. [n: (ISID.)]* No rich man shall enter, that is, no one trusting in riches, as Jesus expounds it according to Mark.

VERS. 25.-- *They wondered.* Because they counted in the number of the rich all who love riches, even if they do not have them. For otherwise, since the crowd of the poor is greater, they would not say: *Who shall be able to be saved?*

VERS. 26.-- *God.* Who turns them from the love of earthly things to the charity of eternal things: not that the covetous and the proud enter.

VERS. 28.-- *In the regeneration.* There are two regenerations, the first of water and of the Holy Spirit, the second in the resurrection. So there are two adoptions and two resurrections. *The Son of man.* That is, when the form of a servant [0149D] which was judged shall have exercised judicial power, you also shall be judges with me. *Upon twelve seats.* By the twelve seats, the whole company of those who judge. By the twelve tribes is understood the whole company of those who are to be judged. Those who left all things and followed the Lord, these shall be judges: those who, having lawful goods, used them rightly, shall be judged, to whom it shall be said: *Come, ye blessed of my Father: For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat.* For there are two orders of the good.

VERS. 29.-- *A hundredfold.* That is, he who shall have left carnal things for the Lord shall receive spiritual things, which in comparison and by their own worth will be such as if a hundred were set against a small number. Mark says: *A hundred times as much now in this time, with persecutions, brethren and [0150A] sisters, and in the world to come life everlasting [n: (Marc. X)]*, that is, in this life full of persecutions they taste beforehand the joy of the kingdom, and enjoy the sincere love of all the elect. But because many grow lukewarm or fall back, he adds: *But many shall be first [n: (Luc. XV)]*, etc.



## CHAPTER XX.

VERS. 1.-- *The kingdom is like.* He shows by a parable that the first shall be last, and the last first. This father of the household is our Creator, who has a vineyard, the universal Church, which from Abel to the last of the elect who is to be born at the end has sent forth as many branches as it has brought forth saints. This father went out to dress his vineyard in the morning, at the third hour, the sixth, the ninth, the eleventh he hired workmen, from the beginning of this world to its end: he does not cease to send preachers to school the people of the faithful. [0150B] *The kingdom is like.* Not to the man only, but to the whole business carried on by the man, and so likewise in like cases. *Early in the morning.* Plainly he began from the first just man to invite preachers, with an everlasting wage, to plant the Church.

VERS. 2.-- *By agreement.* That is, by a confirmed promise that they should be reformed to the image of God, if by building up the Church they should press on in the commandments of the decalogue.

*For a penny. [n: (HIER.)]* The penny bears the image of the king, etc., *as far as* or in your last days come to your senses.

*From the last even unto,* etc. Because those who at the Lord's coming have been called to the kingdom arrive without any lateness, equal to those who began from the beginning of the world, all indeed have the same heaven, but star differs from star in brightness. He began from the last, when he brought the thief into paradise [0150C] before Peter. Because those who come late are sometimes rewarded first, because they go forth out of the body before those who were called in boyhood.

VERS. 15.-- *Or is it not lawful.* A foolish question against the goodness of God. The thing to be asked would be, not whether he gave what he did not owe: but whether he did not give what he did owe. *Is thy eye,* etc. Truly the Jews had a crooked intent, who forbade the apostles to speak to the Gentiles, that they might be saved.

VERS. 16.-- *So the last shall be first. [n: (AUG.)]* That is, the Jews shall be turned from the head into the tail: and the Gentiles from the tail into the head. Whence Moses in the book of Deuteronomy: *The stranger that sojourneth with thee shall go up above thee: he shall be for the head, and thou shalt be for the tail.* But yet [0150D] neither all the first nor all the last belong to the number of the elect.

VERS. 18.-- *Behold we go up,* etc. [n: (HIER.)] This he had often told them, etc., *as far as* let them not doubt that he would rise again.

VERS. 19.-- *To be mocked,* etc. Therefore the Lord would not prosper in the world but suffer heavy things, that he might show us who fell through delight with what bitterness we ought to return.

VERS. 20.-- *Then came to him.* Having heard of the resurrection she thought that he would reign on the spot (forgetful of the second coming), and with a woman's greed she desires things present, forgetful of things to come.

VERS. 21.-- *Say that,* etc. A good desire, but [0151A] an unconsidered petition. And therefore not the will, not the purpose is blamed, but the ignorance: and if simplicity ought not to obtain what it asks, it does not deserve to be put to confusion.

VERS. 22.-- *You know not.* You who ask or seek the seat of glory which you have not yet deserved, the summit of honour delights those whom the way of labour has not yet exercised. *You can.* And this he knew, that they were able to imitate his passion; but he says this so that, with him questioning and them answering, we may all hear: that no one can reign with Christ unless he has imitated his passion.

VERS. 23.-- *The chalice.* As James was beheaded by Herod, and John was sent into a cauldron of boiling oil and banished to Patmos, martyrdom was not wanting to his mind. *It is not mine to give.* That is, the kingdom of heaven is not the giver's but the receiver's. *For there is no respect of persons [0151B] with God:* but whosoever is worthy receives that which is prepared not for the person, but for the life. If therefore you are such as may obtain it, you shall receive what the Father has prepared for the victors. Or, it is not mine to give to the proud, which you still are, but to others for whom it is prepared. Therefore be not you either what you are, but be others, that is, be humbled, you who already wish to be exalted, and it is prepared for you.

VERS. 24.-- *And the ten hearing it.* As those asked carnally to be above all, so these too were carnally grieved that anyone should be before them.

VERS. 30.-- *And behold two blind men.* Of these Mark commemorates one, because he had been most famous in that city: who, cast out from great prosperity, was of a most notorious misery. Blind indeed and a beggar, whence he records both his name [0151C] and the name of his father, Bartimeus the son of Timeus, which does not easily occur in the others, save in Jairus, who was noble in that place too. But the notoriety of the man enlightened won great fame for the miracle. Coming to Jericho he enlightens one, which Luke tells, because drawing near to death he preached the light of the Gospel to the Jews, going out, two, because after the resurrection to the Jews and to the Gentiles. Of whom Mark sets down one, who writes to the Gentiles.



## CHAPTER XXI.

VERS. 1.-- *And when they drew nigh.* Here Matthew passes over the things that were done before he entered Jerusalem, which the others treat at greater length. *And when they drew nigh.* The Lord drew nigh to Jerusalem [0151D] spiritually when he was made flesh, he visited the Church, in which is the vision of peace, and reconciled her to himself by confession. For Bethphage is called the house of the mouth. *Bethphage.* Bethphage was a hamlet of priests on mount Olivet, on the side of which mountain is the town of Bethany. Bethphage, the house of the mouth. Bethany, the house of obedience. These the Lord, journeying to Jerusalem, exalts by his presence, because before his passion he filled many by his teaching with the gifts of devout confession and of obedience. And those towns are set on the mount of Olives, that is, in Christ the Lord, from whom anointing and light come to all; whence: *A city cannot be hid, set upon a mountain.--To mount Olivet: then Jesus,* etc. Looking to the loftiness of mercy, [0152A] ἔλεος is interpreted *mercy.* The nature of oil is to be the servant of light, and the solace of labours and of pains, and it excels the other liquids. *He sent.* Because he does not wish the lamp which he received to be hidden under a bushel. *Two disciples.* Two, as being about to preach the knowledge of truth and cleanness of work, and the sacrament of the twofold love. Some say that these two are Peter and Philip, who first brought Gentiles to Christ, Philip, Samaria, which they interpret as the *she-ass*, Peter, Cornelius, as it were the colt of Samaria.

VERS. 2.-- *And the colt.* The colt is the people of the Gentiles, on which none of the teachers had put the bridle of correction, free and wanton, which itself also was ensnared in the bonds of sins. *For all have sinned and need the grace of God [n: (Rom. III)]* [var: Vulg. Rom 3:23 *egent gloria Dei*, "need the glory of God"]. Others, of the colt only: Matthew, [0152B] who writes to the Hebrews, speaks also of the she-ass, teaching that salvation is not to be despaired of for the Hebrews if they repent. Mark says that the colt was found before the gate where two ways met. The gate is Christ, outside which the people of the Gentiles stood bound: not in the one way of faith, but in divers errors.

VERS. 5.-- *Tell ye the daughter of Sion.* The daughter of Sion is Jerusalem, set on mount Sion. Mystically. The Church belonging to the Jerusalem above, which is the mother of us all, of which no small part was then in the people of Israel. *King.* Lest you say: *We have no king but Caesar [n: (Joan. XIX)]*. *To thee.* If thou believest; against thee if thou believest not. *Upon a she-ass,* etc. He did not sit upon both according to the letter, but in the hearts of both peoples. The Lord could go up upon both, coming down from the one, and going up upon [0152C] the other.

VERS. 7.-- *And they brought.* So the apostles also loosed the world by the power of Christ from the power of the devil, and laid their garments upon it. But the rest of the crowd, that is, the Jews, strew their garments, that is, the commandments of the law, because they were to be trodden underfoot by Christians, in the way, that is, in Christ. *Upon them.* The garments of the apostles are the divine precepts and spiritual grace, by which the foulness of our flesh is covered. Naked of these before, but now adorned by the apostles, the peoples have Christ for their rider. The lesser crowd does not put its garments upon the she-ass, but in the way, and not where he might stumble: because the holy martyrs, putting off the flesh, prepare a way for the simpler sort by the example of their own blood.

VERS. 8.-- *Branches from the trees,* etc. They cut branches or [0152D] leafy boughs, because they culled words and sentences, or examples, from the books of the Fathers.

VERS. 9.-- *Osanna. [n: (HIER.)]* Osi, that is, save, make safe. Anna is the interjection of one entreating, as though, save, I beseech. Osanna is wholly Hebrew, and it signifies that the coming of Christ is the salvation of the world: whence there follows: *Blessed. Osanna,* that is, save. *In the highest.* Because the coming of Christ is the salvation not of men only but of the whole world, joining earthly things to heavenly, *that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, of things on earth, and of things under the earth [n: (Phil. II)]*. *In the highest.* Because it is the salvation of the angels also, whose number he fills up.

VERS. 10.-- *When he had entered.* He entered the city of Jerusalem often, but not with these praises: [0153A] he is not called king, which he had always fled, save only now when he goes up to suffer. And this was done for this reason, that he might the more stir up their envy against himself, because the time of the passion was now at hand.

VERS. 12.-- *And he cast out. [n: (AUG.)]* He had cast them out at another time before, which John alone tells: but of this last casting out the others also speak. *The tables of the money-changers.* Because they came to the temple from all quarters, the priests sold all the animals to those who had them not, even the doves which the poor were to offer, so that afterwards, when these had been sold, they might get back the offerings. But because some had nothing wherewith to buy, they set up money-changers who might make loans: and because the law forbids usury, in its place they took various kinds of goods, that is, apples, grapes and the like; these he casts out. So too mystically he casts them daily out of [0153B] the Church. And he holds guilty of one and the same crime both those who sell and those who buy ecclesiastical offices. *And the chairs of them that sold.* Which belong to the masters, that is, he destroys the priesthood of those who take a price for the laying on of the hand, by which the Holy Spirit is given. Hence it is that the heresy of Simon is condemned. But according to the letter it is absurd to say that dealers in doves sat in chairs.

VERS. 13.-- *Of thieves.* He is a thief who follows after gain, who both persecutes bodily those who do not give, and slays spiritually those who do give, and while he plots the hurt of his neighbour, sits like a thief in a den.

VERS. 14.-- *And there came.* Mystically. He daily heals simple sinners coming to him by penance, enlightening them first when they are blind [0153C] in knowledge and lame in work, and directing them into the life of uprightness.

VERS. 15.-- *The wonderful things which,* etc. That by the scourge of one man, and he of low account, so many should be cast out and the tables overturned, than which he did nothing more wonderful. Something fiery and starlike shines out from his eyes, the majesty of the godhead gleams in his face.

VERS. 16.-- *He said to them.* He does not lie open to a false charge, he does not say, they do well or ill, or, spare their age, but he holds the mean, and, himself keeping silence, confirms the words of the children by the testimony of Scripture. *Of infants and sucklings.* Witnesses of the miracles. They are called Christ's infants, not by age, but by simplicity. Sucklings, as delighted, so to speak, by milk, that is, by the sweetness of the miracles, which are called milk, whereas bread is perfect doctrine.

VERS. 17.-- *He went forth abroad.* Because he was poor and flattered [0153D] no man, he found no host in so great a city, but was received in the house of Lazarus.

VERS. 19.-- *The fig tree.* As he said many things in parables, so he also did them. For why should he seek fruit on a fig tree whose season anyone would know was not yet come, and for that condemn it to everlasting barrenness, unless it were that he here terrified by a deed the people whom he was teaching by word; lest anyone having leaves, that is, words of justice without the fruit of works, should deserve to be cut down. *Leaves.* The traditions of the Pharisees without the fruit of truth, whence another evangelist: the time of the salvation of Israel was not yet, because the people of the Gentiles had not yet come in, or because the time of faith has passed by, when, being despised, he went over to the Gentiles. *Never fruit from thee.* The Creator does no wrong [0154A] to the possessor if he uses his own creature at his own will, and for the profit of others.

VERS. 20.-- *And seeing it.* Since the Lord was to suffer and to bear the scandal of the cross, he had to mark the minds of the disciples by the anticipation of a sign, whence they wondered too that the fig tree had withered: he could by the same power have dried up his enemies, had he not by his patience awaited their salvation.

VERS. 21.-- *Faith.* He has perfect faith who works by love: he can remove mountains. Others obtain pardon of sin if they themselves forgive others.

VERS. 22.-- *You shall receive.* Even if it be deferred to a fitting time, and even if not to those for whom it is asked, yet to those who ask worthily.

[0154B]VERS. 24.-- *I will ask,* etc. He could have refuted them openly: but he asks for this reason, that they may be condemned either by their own silence or by their own sentence, and may know of themselves by what power he does this, according to that saying: *God shall break their teeth in their mouth.*

VERS. 27.-- *Neither do I tell you.* For two causes the truth is hidden, either because the hearers are not capable, whence: *I have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now;* or because they are despisers, whence *Give not that which is holy to dogs.*

VERS. 28.-- *A certain man had two sons, and coming,* etc. When he had made a wary answer to the priests, he at once brings in a parable, both to convict them of impiety and to teach that the kingdom of God is to be carried over to the Gentiles.

[0154C]VERS. 31.-- *They say to him.* In certain codices there stands, *instead of* the first, the last. For they understand the truth, but by shifting about they are unwilling to say what they think, as in the case of John's baptism.

VERS. 32.-- *John in the way of justice.* The Jews, despising John, neither grasped the way of justice, nor did penance for their evil works. *But you. [n: (GREG.)]* Because they were unwilling to answer wisdom openly, they are caught in parables.

VERS. 33.-- *A vineyard.* Of which Isaias [n: (cap. IV)]. *The vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth,* etc. *He dug in it a winepress.* By the digging fear is marked, because they kept those commandments of the law not out of love but out of fear.

VERS. 34.-- *When the time of the fruits drew nigh,* [0154D] etc. Rightly the time of the fruits, not of the fruit: because there was none in that stubborn people.

VERS. 37.-- *Last of all,* etc. See the patience of the father of the household, who waits for repentance. *They will reverence.* As though, I shall do what is mine, let them see to what is theirs.

VERS. 38.-- *This is the heir.* It is plain that the chief priests killed Jesus not through ignorance but through envy, since they knew him to be the one to whom it is said: *Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thine inheritance [n: (Psal. II)]*; whence also, taking counsel for themselves, they said: *If we let him alone so [n: (Joan. II)]*, etc. *We shall have his inheritance.* The inheritance of Christ, which he possessed in rising again, is the Church, which the Jews were striving to snatch away: [0155A] while, his faith being put out, they endeavoured to persuade the Gentiles of the justice that is of the law.

VERS. 39.-- *They cast him forth out of the vineyard.* Mark changes this order, saying: *They killed him and cast him forth out of the vineyard [n: (Luc. XX)]*, as a worthless corpse. In which he marks their obstinacy, because when the Lord had been killed and raised again, they shut him out from their own borders and sent him to the Gentiles.

VERS. 42.-- *The builders.* Who seemed to be building a house for God, as it were, out of the people subject to them.

*And he that shall fall,* etc. He who believes and yet sins: the stone falls upon him and he is not ground to powder, but he is bound tight, because through patience he is kept for salvation; but he upon whom the stone rushes down, that is, he who denies, is utterly ground to powder, so that not even a shard remains; or it falls upon [0155B] him who now despises and does injuries, and he has not yet utterly perished, but is shaken so that he does not walk upright. The stone falls upon him when, coming in judgment, it crushes him, when he says: *Go into everlasting fire.* [var: Vulg. Mt 25:41 *Discedite a me maledicti in ignem aeternum*, "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire"]



## CHAPTER XXII.

VERS. 2.-- *It was made like.* Again he convicts them by parables: he is not silent because they are exasperated, but by another parable he tells them that a worse anger of God is to come. *A marriage feast.* The bridal chamber of the marriage is the virgin's womb. Of those invited to the marriage Matthew alone tells. Luke tells another likeness in part, of a supper, that is, of the eternal banquet, from which no one who has entered is driven out, as he is from the present Church.

[0155C]VERS. 4.-- *The oxen.* Because first the prophets, and afterwards the apostles, suffered from unbelievers: who are now to you for an example of what you must believe. Come, by faith, by agreeing with the rest. The oxen are the fathers of the Old Testament, to whom leave was granted to strike their enemies as with a horn. The fatlings, from feeding, that is, the heralds of the New Testament, fat with inward charity, seeking things on high on the wing of contemplation. Slain, either from what they had been, or already set in rest through the death of the flesh.

VERS. 5.-- *Another to his farm.* To go to a farm is to lie immoderately upon earthly labour. But to trade is to gape after earthly gains.

VERS. 7.-- *And the king.* Above, he was a man while he was inviting and doing works of clemency, now in taking vengeance he is king only [0155D]. *And having sent,* etc. Having sent his armies, that is, the angels by whom he will exercise judgment, he destroys the persecutors: and the city, that is, the flesh in which they dwelt, he will burn with the soul in hell.

VERS. 8.-- *The marriage indeed is ready.* The whole sacrament of the incarnation is accomplished, the nativity and the passion.

*To the outgoings,* etc. Actions are the ways: the outgoings are the failing of actions: because for the most part those are easily converted whom no prosperity attends in earthly doings.

VERS. 11.-- *That he might see the guests.* [var: Vulg. Mt 22:11 *ut viderent discumbentes*, plural, "that they might see"] That is, that he may make the merits of those to be judged be seen, and may discern them. *Not clothed with a wedding garment.* Now, the Pharisees having been refuted, he adds [0156A] that not all who are in the Church are worthy of the kingdom, lest his own grow slothful.

VERS. 12.-- *Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment?* A friend, because invited to the marriage. *How,* he convicts him of shamelessness.
