VERS. 13.-- *His hands and feet being bound.* They are bound by punishment who here would not be bound from evil, that is, restrained. The hands which were not stretched out to almsgiving. The feet slow to good. There each several member shall be subjected to punishments, which here served each several vice. *Outer,* etc. Because here they have the inward darkness of the heart.

VERS. 14.-- *But many are called, but few chosen.* [var: Vulg. Mt 22:14 *Multi enim sunt vocati*, "for many are called"] One being cast out, in whom the whole body of the wicked is set forth, a general sentence is brought in. *But many [0156B] are called.* As though he should say: Even if I have spoken of one, it is to be understood of many.

VERS. 16.-- *With the Herodians, saying.* As though to men unknown, that they might the more easily deceive, because they feared the crowds. What they dare not by themselves, they attempt by the governor's hands. *With the Herodians.* That is, with the soldiers of Herod. Under Caesar Augustus, when the enrolment was made, Judea was made tributary. Over these tributes was set Herod the son of Antipater, an alien and a proselyte, appointed king for the Jews by Augustus. There was therefore sedition among the people, some saying that tributes ought to be given, for security and quiet, since the Romans bear arms for all. The Pharisees striving against it, that the people of God, which pays tithes and the rest that the law prescribes, ought not to lie under human laws. The Pharisees therefore send [0156C] to see whether they might deceive him.

*Thou hast no care,* etc. To this they provoke him, that he should fear God more than Caesar: and therefore should say that tributes ought not to be paid, so that the Herodians might hold him as the author of sedition.

VERS. 18.-- *Hypocrites.* Because they are one thing and feign another.

VERS. 21.-- *Render therefore.* Or, as Caesar exacts the stamping of his own image, so also does God the soul signed with the light of his countenance.

VERS. 23.-- *Sadducees,* etc. There were two heresies among the Jews. That of the Pharisees, who set forward the justice of traditions and observances: and that of the Sadducees, who also claimed for themselves what they were not yet, that is, [0156D] just men. For Sadducees is interpreted *just men*, they do not believe the resurrection of bodies, and think that souls perish with the body, they invent the foulness of a fable to convict of raving those who assert the resurrection. But it may be that this once happened among their nation.

VERS. 29.-- *You err.* For this reason, because you know not the Scriptures, Whence there follows, that they know not the power of God.

VERS. 30.-- *In the resurrection.* Bodies shall indeed rise which could marry and be given in marriage: which is said of those who have the members of generation: but for another reason they shall not marry.

VERS. 31.-- *Have you not read.* In Moses, whom you receive, otherwise he could have given plainer testimonies of the resurrection [0157A] from the prophets: but the Sadducees do not receive the prophets.

VERS. 32.-- *The God of Abraham,* etc. Who were already dead when he said these things, therefore by this he proves that souls remain after death: for he would not be called the God of those that do not exist. And thus the resurrection of bodies also is brought in, which together with the souls did good or evil: *The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.* By this he proves the eternity of souls, and at once brings in: *He is not the God of the dead,* etc., so that when he had proved that souls remain after death, the resurrection of bodies also, which together with the souls did good or evil, might consequently be brought in.

VERS. 34.-- *Silence.* Note that the poisons of envy can be overcome, but with difficulty are laid to rest. *They came together.* [0157B] That by their multitude they might overcome him whom they could not by reason. In tempting him those come together who in doctrine are contrary to one another. They had already been refuted in the showing of the penny, they had already seen the Sadducees too struck dumb, but yet ill-will and spite nourish shamelessness.

VERS. 35.-- *Tempting him.* Mark says that the Lord said to him, when he had answered wisely: *Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.* For it could come to pass that he who came tempting was converted by the Lord's answer. Or the temptation is not an evil one, as of a man wishing to deceive, but by reason of a man wishing to try out further what he does not know.

VERS. 37.-- *Thou shalt love the Lord thy God.* With his first answer the Lord strikes the feigned conscience of the questioner. *Thy God is one. Thou shalt not take the name of thy God in vain. Observe the day of the sabbath.* These three belong to the love [0157C] of God: That thou shouldst think upon his unity, his truth, his will. *With thy whole heart.* The integrity of faith is expressed. In the whole soul, perfect obedience is required. In the whole mind, perseverance is shown.

VERS. 42.-- *Of Christ.* Whether he has come, or whether you believe he is to come, whom you assert to be mere man.

VERS. 44.-- *He said.* To say that is to beget a Son equal to himself. *To my Lord.* Not according to that whereby he was born of him, but according to that whereby he always was of the Father.

VERS. 45.-- *How.* These things are contradictory according to your understanding.

VERS. 46.-- *And no man could,* etc. Note that the poisons of envy can be overcome, but with difficulty are laid to rest.



## CHAPTER XXIII.

[0157D]VERS. 1.-- *Then he spoke.* Those being refuted who are crafty, he instructs those who are fit, none the less exhorting them to be subject to those men for the sake of the priesthood and the dignity of the name: considering not their works, but their teaching.

VERS. 4.-- *Heavy burdens.* The commandments of the law, with their own traditions mixed in, persuading men to live according to these: and not to come to the easy and delightful grace of Christ; whence above: *Come to me, you that labour and are burdened.*

VERS. 5.-- *But all things.* He said that such teachers are to be heard, not imitated: now he shows the cause for which they cannot believe Christ, that is, because they do all things to be seen of men. For he who [0158A] desires earthly glory cannot believe Christ preaching heavenly things.

VERS. 8.-- *But you.* For a twofold reason he bids us take heed of them, lest we be led astray by their dissembling, or lest we be inflamed with emulation.

VERS. 9.-- *One is.* Who enlightens man, which no other man does, but only trains him, by teaching he does not bestow understanding. *Your Father.* God is called Father and Master by nature, man by indulgence. Father, that honour may be paid to age, not that he be held the author of life. Master, from fellowship with the true Master, as his messenger: and he is honoured out of reverence for him by whom he is sent.

VERS. 13.-- *You shut.* Either by evil example, or by taking away the mysteries of the Scriptures. For by the example and [0158B] teaching of those who are masters, others indeed do not receive Christ.

VERS. 15.-- *You go about.* In the whole world you disparage the Gospel: and if anyone cleaves to you, he is the son of a twofold punishment: because he neither receives the remission of sins, and he falls into the fellowship of those who have persecuted Christ. Everyone is called the son of him whose works he does. *a proselyte.* Proselytes are those received from among the Gentiles into the Synagogue, whose rarity is signified by the one, because scarcely any after Christ.

VERS. 16.-- *Whosoever.* The Pharisees, who did all things for gain, used to say that the offerings were even holier than the temple or the altar: so that men might be readier to offer gifts than to pour out prayers in the temple or to do works of justice. In which [0158C] they were looking not to the fear of God, but to their own greed. Therefore the Lord convicts them of folly and of fraud.

VERS. 22.-- *By heaven.* By the creature: where you do not think there is any perjury, he swears by heaven, that is, he swears by the creature that is subject, and by the divinity that presides over the creature.

VERS. 23.-- *Woe to you.* Here too he convicts them of avarice: because they pass over nothing of the things that are for their own advantage. *You that tithe.* Because God had commanded the tithes of all things to be offered for the sustenance of the priests. Note that by almsgiving no impunity is bought for those who remain in iniquity.

[0158D] *These things ye ought.* Lest he should seem to spurn alms, the fruit of the earth, he added these words.

VERS. 24.-- *Blind guides.* Under the opinion of religion you show diligence in the least things which have gain in them: but the great commandments concerning judgment, faith and mercy you devour and neglect. *Straining out.* Mystically. By the name of the gnat the seditious murderer Barabbas is signified: because this creature disquiets by its buzzing and delights in blood. By the name of the camel, for its lowliness in taking up burdens, the Lord is understood. The Jews therefore strain the gnat, that is [sic: *in est*], they observe the least things, because they let Barabbas go, who had not broken the sabbath, and they swallow the camel, that is, they despise the greater things: because they killed Christ, who was setting forth the sabbath spiritually through judgment and [0159A] mercy and faith (which things they despise).

VERS. 25.-- *Woe to you.* By divers likenesses he convicts the pharisees of dissembling and of lying, who show one thing to men and do another at home. *You that make clean.* In vain do you hold out holiness outwardly, as if a man should cleanse a cup on the outside, but leave the filth within: whereas the use of it is within. Luke thus. *Fool, he that made that which is without made also that which is within [n: (Luc. XI)]* [var: Vulg. Lc 11:40 *Stulti nonne qui fecit quod deforis est, etiam id quod deintus est fecit?*, a question addressed to many: "Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make also that which is within?"], that is, he who made both natures of man willed both to be cleansed. Let no one therefore think that fornication and bodily vices of this kind are alone grievous, and that avarice, and pride, and wrath, and the other spiritual vices are light.

VERS. 26.-- *Of the cup.* By way of likeness, not that [0159B] their superstition is in the cup and the dish.

VERS. 29.-- *You that build.* You raise up a memorial of the slain for the favour of the common people, that you may seem just, you even accuse the crimes of your fathers.

VERS. 31.-- *Wherefore.* Because you detest the crimes of your fathers under an appearance indeed of holiness; while by persecuting Christ and the apostles you do the same things, you prove by the deed that you are their sons not only in flesh, but in wicked imitation: and it is plain that they sin knowingly. That is, you speak against yourselves while you condemn your fathers: for you do the like.

VERS. 32.-- *And you.* When it has been proved that they are the sons of murderers, he sets down that to which he was tending: *And fill you up,* fill up what was lacking to them, they slew the prophets, do you slay the Lord of the prophets. He does not command, but shows what [0159C] they are about to do.

VERS. 33.-- *How will you flee. [n: (HIER.)]* By building the sepulchres of the saints, or rather by cleansing your hearts from malice. Will the saints, whose sepulchres you adorn, set you free? Certainly not. The saints are not friends to the enemies of God: in vain do they honour the saints who despise holiness.

VERS. 34.-- *Wise men.* Who know what discourse they utter. *Scribes.* Men skilled in the law.

VERS. 35.-- *That upon you may come.* He speaks not of these present only, but of the whole generation of the wicked, going before and to come: because all are one city, one body of the devil. *Of just Abel.* The justice of Abel was approved by the acceptance of his gifts. *Even to the blood.* Why only thus far, since many were slain after him [0159D] before the birth of Christ, and, when Christ was born, the children were straightway destroyed by this generation? But because Abel was a shepherd of sheep and was slain in the field: Zacharias a priest was slain in the court of the temple: he willed to signify under their names the martyrs of both ranks, both laymen and those bound to the office of the altar. Zacharias, who was slain by king Joas between the temple and the altar, as the history of the Kings relates, was the son of Joiada, and in the Gospel which the Nazaraeans use, instead of the son of Barachias there is read the son of Joiada. But that the justice of Joiada the priest may be proclaimed, he himself is called Barachias, that is, blessed of the Lord. This Zacharias was one of the twelve prophets, as the father of John was one of the prophets.

[0160A]VERS. 36.-- *Upon the generation.* Which is reckoned from the first parricide to the last son of perdition: as though, they shall be alike in punishment as they are also in guilt.

VERS. 37.-- *Jerusalem.* As though he should say: You are guilty of blood, and deservedly, because many times I sent to gather you, and you would not. *How often.* As if he should say: I would, and thou wouldst not, and as many as I gathered, I did by my own will, which is always effectual, while thou wouldst not, because thou wast always ungrateful. *A hen.* This creature has great affection toward her young, so that, touched by their weakness, she grows weak, and, covering them with her wings, fights against the kite. So the wisdom of God, made weak through the flesh, protects us and defends us from the devil.

VERS. 38.-- *It shall be left.* The city, stripped of the help of God, [0160B] shall be left to its own dominion, and it is well left desolate, when it is forsaken by God.

VERS. 39.-- *Blessed is he that cometh.* This the crowds said to the Lord as he came to Jerusalem. But that the Lord says this here, when these things are past, compels it to be understood mystically of the coming of his charity, where they shall confess the Son whom they crucified.



## CHAPTER XXIV.

VERS. 2.-- *There shall not be left here a stone upon a stone.* Mystically. When the Lord withdrew from the temple, all the buildings of the law and that framing of the commandments was destroyed, so that nothing can be fulfilled by the Jews. And it was divinely provided that, as the grace of the Gospel increased, that temple with its ceremonies should be taken away, lest [0160C] anyone weak in faith should, while those things stood, have occasion of Judaism. The same who threatened by word showed it by a sign, when he goes out from them after the threat has been made.

VERS. 3.-- *And as he sat.* Where Mark says, *over against the temple.* He sits over against the temple when he discourses of its ruin and of the destruction of the nation, so that the posture of his body also may agree with his words. Mystically. He sits on mount Olivet, that is, remaining at rest in the Church he detests the arrogance of the proud. *Tell us.* Because he had said that all things were to be destroyed, they ask the time and the signs of the destruction. They ask three things: at what time is Jerusalem to be destroyed? when is Christ to come? when is the consummation of the world to come?

VERS. 4.-- *Take heed.* When these things shall come to pass, let us not think [0160D] that the day of the Lord is at hand, the sign of which is plainly set down in what follows. He forearms them lest they be troubled or fail through deception, as through Simon Magus, or through tribulation and persecution, as through Nero. Note that these things which come before the destruction of Jerusalem are like, and almost the same as, those which shall come to pass at the consummation of the world, and he speaks of the one as though of the other.

VERS. 5.-- *many.* When the destruction of Jerusalem was at hand there were many leaders who said that they were Christs, and that the time of liberty was near. Many in the Church in the times of the apostles, who besides other falsehoods said that the day of the Lord was at hand.

VERS. 6.-- *You shall hear.* These things abounded in Judea from the passion of the Lord [0161A] onward: and lest the apostles, terrified by them, should forsake Jerusalem and Judea, they are admonished that the end is not at once, but after forty-two years.

VERS. 8.-- *And all these things.* But all these things are beginnings, not the consummation, being as it were the heralds of Antichrist, or of the destruction of the city. These belong partly to the overthrow of the Jews, partly to the day of judgment, because the apostles asked in that way about both.

VERS. 9.-- *Then shall they deliver you up.* He adds by what desert these things befall the Jews, who after the killing of Christ persecuted the heralds of his name and of his faith.

VERS. 11.-- *And many false prophets.* Some refer this to the overthrow of the Jews. But then among them, because there was no believer to whom the exhortation might be made; this is better taken of the heretics, of whom the [0161B] first was Simon Magus. The last, greater than all, is Antichrist. It is to be diligently considered which of the signs is to be referred to the destruction of the city, and which to the day of the Lord. For the Lord answered concerning the things that were to follow from that time, whether of the destruction of Jerusalem or of his own coming.

VERS. 14.-- *And it shall be preached.* Because the Lord knew that the hearts of the disciples were to be saddened over the destruction and ruin of their own nation, he lifts them up with this consolation, that they might know that far more companions of eternal joy were to be gathered out of the whole world. Hold moreover this sign, that neither the day of the Lord nor the desolation of Jerusalem is at hand before the apostles have been scattered through the whole world, except the two Jameses, who were killed first in Judea. Scattered, I say, so that if they should grieve over the ruin of their own nation, they might have as a solace [0161C] more companions gathered out of every nation.

VERS. 15.-- *The abomination,* etc. Or if it be said of the destruction of the city, the abomination, that is, an idol. For Pilate set the image of Caesar in the desolated temple. Or this is said of the equestrian statue of Hadrian, which stood a long time in the very place of the holy things.

VERS. 16.-- *Then they that are in Judea.* These things were done according to the letter, when, as the extermination of the Jews drew near, all the Christians, warned by an oracle, fled into the kingdom of Agrippa, who was obedient to the Romans.

VERS. 22.-- *And unless.* What hope then is there for the elect, save the grace of God, which gives patience to the godly, that it may the sooner take away power from the ungodly? For by how much this tribulation shall be the heavier, by so much shall it be the more moderate in its shortness. Or by the name [0161D] of days the evils themselves are signified. *Had been shortened.* Not in measure, but in number, lest by the delay of the times the faith of believers be shaken. For these evils shall last three years and a half only. *Behold, here is Christ.* Each several heresy has also its own fixed parts of the world, whence it is said: *Lo here, and lo there.* Or in hidden or in obscure conventicles it deceives the curiosity of men, whence it is said: *Behold, in the chambers, behold, in the desert.* There shall be many who will not believe that Christ is the common salvation of all, but of some only, whence it is said: *here or there.*

VERS. 24.-- *If it could be done.* [var: Vulg. Mt 24:24 *(si fieri potest)*, present indicative, "if it can be done"] That is, if in any way it could come to pass that God's predetermination were changed, and therefore it cannot be understood of the true elect. *The elect.* Not that the divine [0162A] election is made void, but those who by human judgment seem elect.

VERS. 26.-- *Behold, in the desert.* Many also believe that he does not come into the open, but into the desert. Many believe that Christ gave the more secret precepts of the faith to some, not to all, whence it is said, *in the inner chambers. Do not believe,* that Christ is in the desert or in the inner chambers, but that his faith shines clear and manifest from the East to the West among catholics. Let no credit therefore be given to schismatics. By the name of East and West he designates the whole world.

VERS. 31.-- *From the utmost parts of the heavens.* Lest anyone should think that the elect were to be gathered from the four quarters of the earth, and not from all its bounds, and from the inland regions besides, it is added: *From the utmost part of the earth to [0162B] the utmost part of heaven,* that is, from the farthest bounds of the earth straight on to its uttermost limits: where to those who look from far off the circle of heaven seems to rest upon the earth.

VERS. 32.-- *From the tree.* Mystically. From the people of Israel, in whom blindness has happened in part: and it was the fig tree that was condemned. But when out of the dry wood the branch of faith and charity shall have grown green in him, and the leaves, that is, the words of preaching, shall have sprung forth, the summer which is looked for is near, that is, eternal calm and the longed-for newness of those born again. For when at last, unbelief being taken away, all Israel shall be saved, it must not be doubted that the day of judgment is near.

VERS. 35.-- *Heaven and earth.* They shall be made new, the former shape laid aside, but the substance remaining, [0162C] whence it is said: *The earth shall stand for ever.* [var: Vulg. Ecl 1:4 *terra autem in aeternum stat*, present, "the earth standeth for ever"]

VERS. 36.-- *Of the day.* Lest perhaps, when the signs had been heard, they should seek also the fixed limit of that day, he says: Of the last day, after how many years or days it is to come, be not solicitous, it has been defined to no one whether the judgment shall be by day or by night, but the day is spoken of for manifestation, or the night for concealment. *No one knows,* etc. In certain codices there is added, *neither the Son.* Who indeed knows all things with the Father, but does not make men know, as the Apostle says: *That in him are hidden the treasures of wisdom and of knowledge [n: (II Col. II)]*. He does not make it known, because it would be known to no profit. But let us always be uncertain of the coming of the judge, that we may so live every day as though we were to be judged on the next. Nor have the elect angels made anyone know it. Or [0162D] God has granted the knowledge of this day to none of the holy angels, nor to an adopted son, that is, nor to any of holy men.

VERS. 37.-- *But as.* He affirms the suddenness of the day of his coming by very many examples: for he both compared it to the lightning that flies swiftly over all things, and likens it to the days of Noe, or of Lot according to another evangelist.

VERS. 38.-- *Eating and drinking, marrying,* etc. Not foods and marriages, but the immoderate use of lawful things is reproved. After wars, famines, earthquakes, etc., then a short peace shall follow, that the believer may be tried, whether, when the evils are past, he hopes that the judge will come, whence it is said: *For when they shall say peace and security, then shall sudden destruction come upon them [n: (I Thess. V)]*.

[0163A]VERS. 40.-- *Then,* etc. Luke, *in that night,* that is, in that tribulation in which they are tried, in which some stand fast, others fall. *Two shall be.* There are two sorts of the aforesaid in the Church, of those labouring as it were in a field, of those who sincerely announce Christ, and of those who adulterate the word of God.

VERS. 41.-- *Two grinding.* Two sorts of those who follow the round of changeable things, who are designated by the feminine gender, because women are governed by men, by the counsel of their betters. *Two in a bed.* Those who choose leisure and rest, which are signified by the name of the bed, occupied neither with secular nor with ecclesiastical business. *One shall be taken.* He who for God's sake strives to be continent, that living without solicitude he may think on the things that are God's. But he who has chosen the monastic [0163B] life for human praise or through some corruption of vices, shall be left by God. There are no other kinds of men in the Church than these three. Whence Ezechiel saw three men delivered, Noe, Daniel and Job, that is, rulers like Noe, the continent like Daniel, the married like Job. And according to these three kinds of men he sets down three parables. In the first he treats of those labouring in the field, which is where he says: *Watch ye therefore.* In the second he treats of those who are in the bed, which is where he says: *The kingdom of heaven is like to ten virgins.* In the third he treats of those grinding at the mill, which is where he says: *For even as a man going into a far country,* etc.

VERS. 42.-- *Watch ye therefore. [n: (HIER.)]* He did not say, because we know not, but, because you know not, that he might show that he himself is not ignorant of the day of judgment.

[0163C]VERS. 43.-- *If he knew,* etc. The thief breaks through the house while the father of the household knows it not, because while the spirit sleeps from its own guarding, unforeseen death bursts into the dwelling of the flesh, and drags it away to punishment. But he would withstand the thief if he watched, because, guarding beforehand against the coming of the judge who comes secretly, he would meet him by doing penance.

VERS. 45.-- *Who, thinkest thou, is the faithful servant.* By three likenesses, of the lightning, of the thief, and of the drowning of the Pentapolis, he brought in the terror of judgment to all in common, that they might watch and be ready. Now he speaks especially to prelates, who ought to be humble, prudent, not seeking the good for the sake of temporal gain, but to feed the sheep by word and by example and by work. *Who, thinkest thou,* as though he should say: You are to be admonished. For how rare is he that serves the Lord for the Lord's sake, feeding the sheep [0163D] of Christ not for gain, but out of love of Christ. *Prudent.* Providing for himself in what is to come. *Whom he hath appointed.* How rare is he who is called by God as Aaron was and has not rather thrust himself forward, and who does not feed himself rather than the sheep.

VERS. 46.-- *Blessed is that servant.* But he is to be glorified with eternal blessedness who, when the Lord comes to judgment, shall be found faithfully dispensing the allowance of the word and watching in the care of the flock. Rarely is one found faithful or prudent, but he who is found such is blessed.

VERS. 47.-- *Over.* That is, over all the joys of the heavenly kingdom he will make the rest, that is, the good hearers, sit down, and passing by he will minister to them.

VERS. 49.-- *To strike his fellow servants.* To do them injuries, [0164A] or to corrupt the consciences of the weak by a crooked word or example. Whence Luke says *menservants or maidservants [n: (Luc. XII)]*, whose fall is by so much the easier as their age or sex is the weaker.

VERS. 51.-- *With the hypocrites,* etc. With those, namely, who were in the field and who were grinding, and were nevertheless left behind. Who are called hypocrites both in the field and at the mill, that is, who seemed to do good things, but the outcome of a different will appeared. *Weeping* By a likeness of the members the greatness of the torments is shown.



## CHAPTER XXV.

VERS. 1.-- *Ten virgins.* The virgins are all who refrain themselves from the luxury of the world. *And the bride.* All together are the bride, who has now been espoused a virgin away from the corruption of the world. She shall be wedded, when the mortal shall be joined to the [0164B] immortal.

VERS. 2.-- *Five.* Because continence in carnal enticements is fivefold, namely that in the five senses they should refrain themselves from pleasures.

VERS. 5.-- *And the bridegroom tarrying.* Because there is no little time between the first and the second coming of Christ. *They all slumbered and slept.* Because they are afterwards to be raised up.

VERS. 6.-- *And at midnight there was a cry made.* That is, with no one knowing or hoping for it. Whence *The day of the Lord shall come as a thief in the night [n: (I Thess. III)]*.

VERS. 8.-- *Give us of your oil,* etc. Those whose deeds are propped up by what is another's fail when that same praise is withdrawn, and out of habit they always seek that whence the mind is wont to rejoice. And so they wish to have before God, who is the searcher of the heart, the testimony of men, who do not [0164C] see hearts.

*They are going out.* That is, at the coming of the judge they are darkened within, and they have no reward from God, because they have received their praise.

VERS. 9.-- *Lest perhaps.* Because each shall render an account for himself, nor is anyone helped before God by another's testimony, since to him secret things lie open, and each scarcely suffices for himself, that his own conscience may bear him witness. *Lest perhaps* each one shall receive a reward for his own works, nor in the day of judgment can the virtues of some relieve the vices of others. *To them that sell.* They that sell are flatterers, because they give praise and receive some reward.

VERS. 10.-- *But whilst.* While they bend themselves toward [0164D] the things that are without, and seek their accustomed joys, since they have not known the things within, he comes who judges. *It was shut.* After the judgment great is the severity of him whose mercy before it is unspeakable.

VERS. 11.-- *But last of all.* By true penance, by fruitless tears, those left outside knock. It is not said that they bought oil: because, no joy from the praises of others now remaining, in their straits they return to the imploring of God.

VERS. 13.-- *Watch ye.* Namely, that we may prepare for ourselves the testimony of a good conscience, lest with the foolish virgins we remain outside. *You know not the day nor the hour.* Not only the day of judgment, but the day of each man's death, or the hour in which he who is found ready [0165A] shall then also be found ready. And because he desires to find us ready, he adds another parable on the same matter.

VERS. 14.-- *Going into a far country he called his servants,* etc. The place of the flesh is the earth, therefore he led the flesh of Christ, our own, unto foreign parts, when he ascended into heaven.

VERS. 15.-- *And immediately he took his journey.* Not changing place, but allowing them a free power of working.

VERS. 16.-- *He traded with them.* By keeping himself from visible things, by exhorting others as he was able, that they might pass over from visible things to invisible. Or by preaching to both sexes, and by forming them in good morals, he doubled the talents he had received.

[0165B]VERS. 19.-- *But he reckoned.* He began to examine the deeds of each, their conscience accusing or excusing every one.

VERS. 20.-- *Behold other five.* As many as he converted from error, so many he offered to the Lord, his conscience bearing him witness that by the grace given him he not only profited himself, but also gained those whom he could.

VERS. 21.-- *Over a few things.* The good things of the present life are few, although they seem many, because they are not without an admixture of some trouble. But the eternal good things are many, which are without any trouble of corruption. *Enter into the joy of thy Lord.* Mingled with the choirs of angels: so rejoice within over the gift, that there may now be nothing without over which thou shouldst grieve for corruption.

[0165C]VERS. 22.-- *He that had received two talents.* This man by his own powers doubled in the Gospel whatever he had learned in the law of God. Or he understood the conscience and the works of the present life as figures of the blessedness to come.

VERS. 24.-- *Thou art a hard man.* Because the way that leads to life is steep, and because the higher the step, the heavier the fall.

VERS. 25.-- *And being afraid I went away,* etc. And fearing to attempt the step of a higher life, lest, seeking another's salvation, I myself should be endangered. *I hid thy talent.* I did not preach what I understood by thy gift.

VERS. 26.-- *Thou knewest that,* etc. Why did that thought not strike fear into thee, so that thou shouldst know that I would seek my own more diligently? What he said by way of excuse is turned into blame.

[0165D]VERS. 27.-- *To the bankers.* Or to the other teachers, as to the apostles and bishops. Or, to all believers who are able to double the money.

VERS. 28.-- *And give it to him,* etc. We see this for the most part done in the Church, because very many, while they minister well the outward things which they receive, are led on by an added grace to the mystical understanding also.

VERS. 29.-- *For to everyone,* etc. For many, though wise and sharp by nature, if they are slothful, lose the good of nature, and the reward that had been promised them seems to pass over to others, who acquire by industry what they have less of by nature. Or he who has faith and a good will, even if he has less in work, it shall be given to him by the good judge. But he who has it not in faith [0166A] loses even the virtues which he has naturally, without which [faith] there are no virtues. Or he who has love of the word, to him is given the sense of understanding. But he who has it not, even if he is skilled by natural study, fails. Or he who has not charity loses every good that he has. Note that whatever is given to each in worldly or in spiritual things is reckoned for a talent of which he is to render an account.

VERS. 31.-- *And when.* Being about to be delivered to the cross very soon, he set before them the glory of him who triumphs, that he might make up by this promise for the scandals that were to follow. After the parables about the end of the world, the Lord now sets forth the manner of the judgment to come.

VERS. 32.-- *The sheep from,* etc. There shall be two orders in the judgment, namely of the elect and of the reprobate: but of the elect [0166B] some shall judge, to whom it is said: *You also shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the tribes of Israel.* Others shall be judged, to whom it is said: *I was hungry and you gave me to eat.* Likewise of the reprobate, some who are outside the Church shall not be judged: others who shall be judged, to whom it is said: *I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat,* etc.

VERS. 33.-- *The goats.* The he-goat is a butting and rank-smelling animal, which was offered for sins in the law, and it signifies sinners: nor does he say she-goats, which can have young.

VERS. 34.-- *Blessed of the Father.* Advanced by the benefit of my Father to the obtaining of glory, in which you may reign without corruption, to which you have been predestined from the foundation of the world.

[0166C]VERS. 37.-- *Then shall they answer.* Not distrusting the words of the Lord, but either amazed at the greatness of the king's majesty; or because every good thing that they did seems little to them, whence it is said: *The sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come [n: (Rom. VIII)]*, etc.

VERS. 40.-- *Of these brethren.* My brethren and my mother are they who do the will of my Father.

VERS. 42.-- *You gave me not,* etc. What does he deserve who has seized what belongs to another, if he is eternally damned who has not given anything of his own?

VERS. 44.-- *Lord, when,* etc. They busy themselves to excuse themselves, as though they who were deceiving men could deceive God. But they have no excuse who would not be converted from evils and do alms; whence he adds: [0166D] *As long as you did it not to one,* etc.

VERS. 46.-- *Into everlasting punishment.* In vain therefore does Origen promise deliverance after many years to evil men and to the demons themselves. *Into everlasting punishment. [n: (AUG.)]* In which matter Origen was assuredly the more merciful, who believed that the devil himself too and his angels, after punishments heavier according to their deserts and of longer duration, were to be rescued out of those torments and joined to the holy angels. But the Church has not undeservedly condemned him, both for this and for sundry other things, and chiefly for the blessednesses and miseries alternating without ceasing, and for the endless goings and returnings from those to these at fixed intervals of ages.



## CHAPTER XXVI.

[0167A]

VERS. 1.-- *And it came to pass when he had finished.* Concerning the consummation of the world and the separation of the judgment: or, from the beginning of the Gospel until the passion he had accomplished all things by doing and by preaching. After the discourse in which he foretold that he would come in brightness, he showed that he would suffer, that he might give warning that the sacrament of the cross is mingled with the glory of eternity.

VERS. 6.-- *And when.* The counsel having been held, the order of the narrative passes over to that place, *then went one of the twelve,* so that the deed of Judas may be joined to the counsel of the priests. But he returns to that day which was before the six days of the Pasch, saying: *And when,* etc. *Of Simon.* The former name remains, that the power of him who heals may appear. By that house understand that part of the people which believed [0167B] the Lord and was healed. *Simon,* that is, obedient.

VERS. 7.-- *There came near. [n: (HIER.)]* Observe diligently what is said of the two women concerning the head. For indeed the sinful woman, upon the feet, and she who is said not to have been a sinner, upon the head. *A woman having.* Mary Magdalen, the sister of Lazarus, now just and of his household, who once came a sinner and washed his feet with tears, now anointed his head and his feet, the feet now, as John says. *Of precious ointment.* Mark: of spikenard, that is, made of the spikes and the leaves, which is more precious. John, of pistic nard, that is, faithful, not adulterated with other herbs: πίστις in Greek, faith in Latin. *Mystically.* This devotion of Mary signifies the faith of the Church, which, while it preaches the Godhead of Christ, anoints the head: while it preaches his humanity, the feet. Of this ointment in the house of Simon the leper in [0167C] Bethany both Matthew and Mark and John speak. But Luke tells of another thing like to this, done before in the house of another Simon, a Pharisee, not a leper, nor in Bethany, but concerning the same woman who then came a sinner.

VERS. 8.-- *The disciples had indignation.* John says that Judas spoke these things, and this for the sake of covetousness: the others could agree with his words, or even say the same, but out of care for the poor.

VERS. 11.-- *But me,* etc. In bodily presence, otherwise he says elsewhere: *Behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world.*

VERS. 12.-- *For she in pouring.* It is an office of burial, which you think to be waste. Nor is it a wonder if she gives me the odour of faith, for which I am soon to pour out my blood.

[0167D]VERS. 15.-- *What will you give.* Betraying him as though a worthless chattel, he puts it in the power of the buyers how much they will give.

VERS. 17.-- *Where wilt thou,* etc. There was no fixed house for them: wherein the building of superfluous things is condemned.

VERS. 18.-- *To a certain man.* He signifies the same man whom Mark and Luke call the master of the house. He therefore who says to a certain man, as though in his own person (and not the Lord's), for the sake of brevity indicated him in a summary way. *To a certain man.* Not to anyone whatever, but to some certain man, whom, speaking in his own person, he would rightly have set down. But now, when he has set down the words of the Lord, *Go ye into the city:* he himself puts in, *to a certain man:* not [0168A] because the Lord said this, but that he himself might indicate to us, the proper name being left unspoken, that there was there a certain man to whom they were sent.

VERS. 19.-- *And the disciples did even as.* In another Gospel it is written: *They found a large upper room furnished* [var: Vulg. Mc 14:15 *Et ipse vobis demonstrabit coenaculum grande, stratum*, "and he will show you a large upper room furnished"]. The upper room is the spiritual law, which, going forth from the straits of the letter, receives the Saviour in a lofty place. For he who follows the letter keeps the Pasch in the lowest place. But he who follows the water-bearer, that is, the herald of grace, into the house of the Church, he, transcending the letter by the spirit, prepares a refreshment for Christ in the height of the mind.

VERS. 21.-- *That one of you.* He who foretold concerning the passion foretells concerning the betrayer, that seeing himself not to be hidden he might repent of the deed. He casts the charge upon the number, that the guilty one might do [0168B] penance, yet he does not point him out particularly, lest he should become more shameless.

VERS. 22.-- *They began every one.* Because they believe the master more than themselves: and fearing also their own frailty, they ask concerning a sin of which they have no knowledge in themselves.

VERS. 23.-- *He that dippeth.* While the others were made sorrowful and were drawing back their hand from the food, with that shamelessness with which he betrayed him he puts his hand in with the master, that by boldness he might feign a good conscience. Behold the humility and the patience with which he admits the betrayer to the table. *In the dish.* Mark: *in the bowl.* A paropsis is a four-cornered vessel for food, so called from equal apsides, that is, from equal sides: a catinum is an earthen vessel fit for pouring in liquid, and it could happen that the table held a vessel both earthen [0168C] and four-cornered. The penalty is foretold, that the punishments declared might correct him whom shame had not overcome.

VERS. 24.-- *It were better for him.* It would be much better not to be at all than to be in evil case, he says this in the customary and simple way. For it cannot be well with him who is not. Or does he say to the devil, not to be born unto sin: or was it also good for him that he should not be born to Christ by calling, lest he should be an apostate by betrayal? Or we are wont to say simply, it would be better not to be than to be in evil case.

*Rabbi.* The others say, Lord, this man, Rabbi. As though it were a lesser sin to betray a master than the Lord, or else by way of flattery.

VERS. 25.-- *Thou hast said it.* Nor is it openly said here whether [0168D] it was he: for it can be understood as though he were saying, I did not say it.

VERS. 26.-- *And whilst they were at supper,* etc. The solemn joys of the old Pasch being ended, which were kept in memory of the deliverance of the people of God out of Egypt, he passes over to the new, which he willed the Church to frequent in memory of himself. Namely, that in place of the flesh and blood of the lamb he might substitute the sacrament of his own body and blood, and might show that he is the one to whom *the Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: thou art a priest [n: (Psal. CIX)]*, etc. *He took. [n: (HIER.)]* After the typical Pasch had been fulfilled, and he had eaten the flesh of the lamb with the apostles, he takes bread. *And blessed and broke.* Because he so subjected the man he had assumed to death, that he showed the power of immortality [0169A] to be in him, and that therefore he would rise again quickly. *He broke,* that he might show that the breaking of his body would not be without his own will. He blessed first, because the nature which he assumed he filled, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, with the grace of divine power. Therefore he gave his body after supper, because it was necessary that the typical Pasch should first be completed, and that so the sacraments should afterwards be substituted for the old Pasch. But we, for reverence of so great a sacrament, are refreshed with the sacraments of the Lord's passion before bodily food.

VERS. 27.-- *He gave thanks.* He shows what each one ought to do under the scourge of his own fault, since he himself bore with an even mind the scourge of another's: because bread strengthens the body, wine produces blood.

VERS. 29.-- *I will not drink.* I will not take delight in the ceremonies [0169B] of this people, among which the rites of the paschal lamb are chief. After the passion I will not take up flesh, until I take it up new, which is now mortal.

*New in the kingdom of the Father.* Calling that *new,* and this old, he shows the body: namely, that which is of the old Adam, which shall be changed by immortality. *With you,* by this immortality is promised to his own also, although not at the same time. *Of this fruit,* because the same bodies are to rise again. But the day of my resurrection will be when, exalted in the kingdom of God, that is, in the glory of immortality, I shall be filled with a new joy together with you over the salvation of that same people regenerated by spiritual grace.

VERS. 30.-- *And a hymn.* This is what the psalm says: *The poor shall eat and shall be filled [n: (Psal. XXI)]*, etc. Or, according to John, he sang a hymn giving thanks to the Father, [0169C] in which he prayed for himself and for the disciples and for those who should believe. *They went out unto the mount,* etc. That through the receiving of the sacraments and through his own intercession he may teach us to ascend to higher gifts, with which we are anointed in heart: where is the refreshment of labour, the solace of sorrow.

VERS. 31.-- *That you all suffer scandal* [var: Vulg. Mt 26:31 *Omnes vos scandalum patiemini,* "you shall all be scandalized"]. He foretells to them what they are to suffer, that afterwards they may not then despair, but be set free by penance.

VERS. 32.-- *After.* As he foretold the place of the passion, so he foretells the place of the resurrection, that as they are sorrowful from the passion, so they may rejoice, glorified by the resurrection or by the vision. *I will go before you,* etc. That he might console their weakness by the promise of his own return.

[0169D]VERS. 33.-- *And if all.* It is not a lie nor rashness, but faith and burning love, to such a degree that he did not look to his own weakness nor to the trustworthiness of the words of God.

VERS. 36.-- *And pray.* Death being close at hand, he fitly prays in the valley of fatness, because through humility and the fatness of charity he underwent death for us.

VERS. 37.-- *He began to grow sorrowful.* Not from fear of the passion, since he had come for this, but on account of the scandal of the apostles and the perdition of the ungodly. *[n: (HIER.)] He began to grow sorrowful,* that he might prove the truth of the man he had assumed. He was truly made sorrowful, but the passion does not rule over his mind: rather it is a propassion, whence he says: *He began [0170A] to grow sorrowful.* But he is made sorrowful not from fear of suffering, since he had come for this, but on account of the unhappy Judas and the scandal of the apostles and the casting out of the Jews and the overthrow of Jerusalem.

VERS. 38.-- *Sorrowful.* It is the soul that fears and is made sorrowful. Peter, the lesser, does not fear, saying: *I will lay down my life for thee:* because, as a man, he does not know the force of death. Christ fears, because, as God set within a body, he sets forth the frailty of the flesh: he who took a body was bound to undergo all things that belong to a body.

*Even unto death. [n: (HIL.)]* Not because of death, but until he should free the apostles by his own passion. It is not death, but the time of death, that is in fear, because after the power of the resurrection the faith of believers is to be strengthened.

VERS. 39.-- *If it be possible.* This not out of fear, [0170B] but out of mercy, lest the Jews, who have not the excuse of ignorance, should not kill him [cj: *non occidant*; read *occidant*, "should kill him"]; whence he says: *this,* that is, the cup of the people of the Jews, not simply a cup: *If it be possible* that the Gentiles may believe without the destruction of the Jews, I refuse the passion. But if they are to be blinded that the Gentiles may come in, let not my will, but thine be done. *Not as I will. [n: (AUG.)]* He transfigures his own into himself, who wills nothing other than the Father, as in that place: *I was hungry, and you gave me to eat. And why persecutest thou me?* But he teaches them to correct their own private will and to direct it according to the divine. [n: (AMBR.)] The man whom he showed forth by the truth of a body, he made equal in affection, so as to say: *But not as I will, but as thou* [var: Vulg. Mt 26:39 *verumtamen non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu*]. He took up my will, he took up my sorrow. [0170C] Confidently do I name sorrow, I who preach the cross.

VERS. 41.-- *But the flesh.* He says this assuredly not of himself, but of those who said that they would never deny him.

VERS. 42.-- *Again a second time.* He prays a second time, that is, if Nineveh cannot be saved otherwise, unless the gourd wither, that is, the people of the Jews, who before were his tabernacle, so that it may kill me.

VERS. 44.-- *He prayed the third time.* He prayed three times over, that we too may pray for pardon from past sins, and for protection from the evils we repent of, and for wariness against future perils, and that we may direct every prayer to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Likewise, as there is a threefold temptation of desire, so also of fear. For there is the concupiscence of the flesh, the concupiscence of the eyes and the ambition of the world. There is also the fear of death, and the fear of advantage, [0170D] and the fear of pain, against all which he teaches that we ought to be fortified by prayer. Whence also, on account of the threefold temptation of the passion, it can be understood that the Lord prayed three times.

VERS. 47.-- *With swords and clubs.* The deed agrees with the changed mind. For now he comes with clubs who, so long as he was at peace, bore himself more quietly.



## CHAPTER XXVI. (cont.)

VERS. 48.-- *He gave them a sign* [var: Vulg. Mt 26:48 *dedit illis signum*]. He thought that the signs which he had seen were done not by divine power, but by magic: and him whom he had heard was transfigured upon the mountain he feared lest in some such way he should now slip out of their hands: and therefore he gave a sign. *Whomsoever I shall kiss.* He still had something of the modesty of a disciple, in that he did not betray him openly to persecutions, but by the sign of a kiss.

[0171A]VERS. 49.-- *And he kissed him.* The Lord received the kiss, not that he might teach us to dissemble, but lest he should seem to flee the betrayal, whence: *With them that hated peace I was peaceable [n: (Psal. CXIX)]*.

VERS. 52.-- *They shall perish with the sword.* With that sword which, being of fire, is turned before paradise, that is, of divine vengeance, and with the sword of the spirit, that is, of the word of God.

VERS. 53.-- *Thinkest thou that,* etc. As if he should say, I have no need of the help of the twelve apostles, I who can have twelve legions of angels, in which are seventy-two thousand, by which the tongue of all nations is expressed. But he intimates that it is not to be feared if all nations rise up against Jesus, since he himself has far stronger armies of angels. Otherwise: This number signifies the whole race of men [0171B] that was to contend with the Roman empire against the Jews. These are the angels of God, who in the forty-second year after the resurrection, together with Titus and Vespasian, destroyed those murderers and burned their city.

VERS. 55.-- *You are come out with swords.* It is foolish to seek with swords and clubs him who gives himself up of his own accord, and to track down by night through a betrayer, as though he were in hiding, one who taught daily in the temple. But you gather together in the darkness, because your power is in the darkness.

VERS. 57.-- *To Caiphas.* The name agrees with the deed. Caiphas, that is, a searcher out, or shrewd to fulfil, namely, the wickedness of his own guile. Or, one vomiting with the mouth, because he was shameless in uttering a lie and in demanding a murder.

[0171C]VERS. 58.-- *Afar off.* Rightly afar off, he who was about to deny him close at hand, he signifies the Church, which would imitate the passion of Christ far differently, because the Church suffers for itself, but Christ for the Church.

VERS. 64.-- *Thou hast said it.* Mark: *I am:* which is the same: And there is a like answer against Pilate and against Caiphas, that they may be condemned out of their own sentence. *The Son of man.* Me, exalted in the form which you judge, and having the name which is above every name.

VERS. 65.-- *He rent his garments.* The fury which made him rise from his seat makes him also rend his garment. By a great mystery: since the garment of the Lord could not be rent even by the soldiers. For it signifies that their priesthood, the pontificate, was for their crimes to be utterly dissolved: but the solidity [0171D] of the Church (which is called the garment of God) will remain unbroken to the end of the world. It is the custom of the Jews, when they hear anything of blasphemy, they rend their garments.

Which Paul and Barnabas did in Lycaonia, when they were called Jupiter and Apollo.

VERS. 67.-- *Then they spit.* As he was then spit upon with the spittle of unbelievers, so now he is dishonoured with the reproaches of false believers, and is beaten with buffets, that is, with the blasphemies of the same men.

VERS. 68.-- *Prophesy.* They speak an insult to him who willed to be held a prophet by the peoples. For they veiled his face, according to Mark, not that he might not see their crimes, but that they might hide from themselves the grace [0172A] of the knowledge of him. As there was a veil upon the face of Moses, which remains to this day.

VERS. 69.-- *One maidservant.* Why does a maidservant betray him first, when the men were better able to recognize him, unless that this sex might be shown to have sinned unto the death of the Lord: and redeemed through the passion. And therefore a woman first received the mystery of the resurrection: and kept the commands, that she might abolish the old error of the transgression. As through a woman the ancient enemy seduced the first parent, so through a woman he drives the prince of the Church to deny the master whom he had confessed to be Christ the Son of God.

VERS. 72.-- *I know not the man.* How harmful are the conversations of the wicked, which compel Peter to deny Christ, or that he knew the man whom he confessed [0172B] among the disciples to be the Son of God.

VERS. 73.-- *They that stood by.* John and Luke speak of one, a kinsman of Malchus. But either it is a plural for a singular. Or there was one who had seen him and was speaking chiefly, whom the rest, following him, accused in like manner.

VERS. 74.-- *And immediately the cock crew.* After the third denial the cock's crowing follows. The sacraments of things are signified by the state of the times. At midnight he denies, at the cock's crowing he repents, after the resurrection, in the light, he professed three times that he loved him whom he had three times denied: because what he had erred in the darkness of forgetfulness, he corrected by the remembrance of the light already hoped for: and by the presence of that same true light he fully raised up whatever he had changed.

VERS. 75.-- *He remembered.* In another Gospel it is said, [0172C] *The Lord looked upon Peter [n: (Luc. XXII)]*, and by his look drew him to tears, as though bringing back to his mind how often he had denied, and what he had foretold to him, nor could he remain in darkness upon whom the light of the world had looked. *And going forth.* Shut off from the counsel of the ungodly, he washes away his fault, which he did not do within. For this cause he was permitted to waver, that in the prince of the Church a remedy of penance might be established, and that no one should dare to trust in his own strength.



## CHAPTER XXVII.

VERS. 1.-- *And in the morning.* Matthew and Mark have woven together the narrative of the things that were done with the Lord up to the morning, but afterwards they go back to tell the denial of Peter: which being ended, they return [0172D] again to the morning, that from there they might weave together the rest.

VERS. 4. *I have sinned in betraying,* etc. As though it were in his own power to change the sentence of the persecutors: but although he changed his will, yet he did not change the outcome of his first will. *What is that to us.* What does it concern us about this? *look thou to it,* do thou know what thou hast done. Or, what dost thou see as pertaining to us. What does the price received concern us: thou hadst approved of that, do thou with it what thou wilt. They who sin unto death have so great ignorance and blindness that they are neither troubled in their crimes, nor tormented with the pain of repentance.

VERS. 5.-- *And casting down.* As his repentance was fruitless, so also this offering in the temple is execrable. *And going away. [n: (HIER.)]* It profited Judas nothing to have done penance, by which he could not [0173A] correct his crime. But when a brother so sins against a brother that he is able to amend what he has sinned, it can be forgiven him. But if the works remain, penance is taken up with the voice in vain. This is what is said of him: *And let his prayer be turned to sin [n: (Psal. CVIII)]*: so that not only was he unable to amend the wickedness of the betrayal, but he added the crime of his own murder, whence he was the more wicked.

VERS. 6.-- *It is not lawful for them.* Truly straining out the gnat and swallowing the camel: for if for this reason they do not put the money into the corbona, that is, into the treasury, that is, among the gifts of God, because it is the price of blood, why then is the blood itself poured out? And what reward is theirs, if from it a field is bought for the burial of the poor?

VERS. 9.-- *By Jeremias. [n: (HIER.)]* This is read not in Jeremias, but in Zacharias: yet in other words. [0173B] I lately read an apocryphon of Jeremias, in which I found these words written. But nevertheless it seems to me rather that this was taken from Zacharias, after the manner of the apostles, who, the order of the words being passed over, bring forward only the meanings out of the Old Testament.

*Of the children of Israel,* etc. From whom it was less fitting, who ought to have magnified him.

VERS. 11.-- *Thou art the king of the Jews.* According to Luke they had brought two charges, namely that he forbade tribute to be given to Caesar, and that he said he was a king. Concerning the kingdom, therefore, Pilate asks, because he does not know it. Concerning the tributes: because he had heard that he had answered: *Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's [n: (Zac. II)]*: he disregards, as it were, the open lie of the envious. Whence Mark: *And their testimonies were not agreeing [n: (Marc. XXIV)]* [var: Vulg. Mc 14:56 *et convenientia testimonia non erant*, without *eorum*]. In [0173C] this, that Pilate asks of no other crime except whether he is the king of the Jews: the Jews are convicted of impiety, who could not even falsely find what they might lay against the Saviour.

VERS. 16.-- *Who was called Barabbas.* Barabbas, in the Gospel according to the Hebrews, is interpreted *son of the father* or *their master.* He himself is Antichrist, whom they prefer to Christ, to whom it is said: *You are of your father the devil [n: (Joan. VIII)]*. Pilate, who is interpreted *the mouth of the hammerer,* signifies the devil, who is the hammer of the whole earth, by whom the Lord permits his own vessels to be tried: and at the last he grinds him down, when in the final damnation he shall break him in pieces.

VERS. 17.-- *Whom will you.* Wishing to satisfy the people, he gives the choice, although he does not doubt that Christ [0173D] is to be chosen, knowing that he had been handed over through envy. *Who is called Christ.* The same as what Mark says: the king of the Jews, whose king Christ was called.

VERS. 19.-- *For the judgment seat.* The tribunal is the seat of judges, as the throne is of kings, the chair of teachers. *His wife.* The wife of a Gentile man understands in a vision that which the Jews, waking, would not understand. *Have thou nothing to do with that just man.* Now at last the devil, understanding that through Christ he was to lose his spoils, just as at the first he brought in death through a woman; so now through a woman he wishes to free Christ out of the hands of the Jews, lest through his death he lose the empire of death.

VERS. 21.-- *Barabbas,* etc. They chose the son of the devil instead of the Son of God, that they might destroy the Saviour together with their own salvation, [0174A] and set free a betrayer, which petition of theirs cleaves to them even to this day, their nation and their place and their liberty being lost: because they willed to destroy the giver of liberty.

VERS. 22.-- *What therefore shall I do with Jesus.* He sought many occasions to set him free with the goodwill of the people. First, comparing a robber with a just man. Then: *What then shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?* [var: Vulg. Mt 27:22 *Quid igitur faciam de Jesu, qui dicitur Christus?*; Migne's own lemma above prints *igitur*] And when they said: *let him be crucified,* he did not at once yield, but according to his wife's suggestion he says: *Why, what evil hath he done?* By which saying Pilate absolved Christ.

VERS. 24.-- *He washed his hands.* Signifying the Gentile people, a stranger to the impiety of the Jews, who cried out: *Crucify him, crucify him.*

VERS. 25.-- *His blood.* The imprecation persists to this day, and the blood of Christ is not taken away [0174B] from them.

VERS. 26.-- *Then he released to them Barabbas.* Barabbas, a seditious robber and the author of murders, was released to the people of the Jews. [n: (ISID.)] The devil, who long since had for his pride been driven out of the fatherland of light, and had been sent into the prison of darkness. And therefore the Jews cannot have peace, because they chose rather the prince of seditions. Or, Barabbas bore the type of Antichrist.

*But Jesus having been scourged* [var: Vulg. Mt 27:26 *Jesum autem flagellatum*]. Therefore it is to be believed that Pilate scourged Jesus and gave him to the soldiers to be mocked, that the Jews, sated with his punishments and his reproaches, might thirst no further for his death. *But Jesus.* Serving the Roman laws, which command that those who are to be crucified be first scourged.

[0174C]VERS. 28.-- *A scarlet cloak. [n: (HIER.)]* In the scarlet cloak he bears up the bloody works of the Gentiles. In the crown of thorns he looses the ancient curse. In the reed he kills the venomous beasts. Or he holds the reed in his hand, that he might write the sacrilege of the Jews. He is not mocked in his own garments, but in those which he bore for our sins. When he was crucified he received his own adornment at once: because the elements are troubled, and the creature gives testimony to the Creator.

VERS. 32.-- *A man of Cyrene.* Behold, not a Hebrew, but a foreigner is put under the reproach of Christ, that the fulness of the sacraments might be shown to pass over from circumcision to uncircumcision.

VERS. 33.-- *Golgotha.* It is Syriac, and is interpreted *of Calvary,* not because of the baldness of Adam, whom they falsely say was buried [0174D] there, but because of the beheading of the condemned. Adam is read in the book of Josue to have been buried near Hebron.

VERS. 34.-- *Mingled with gall.* Another evangelist says *myrrhed,* that is, most bitter. And there could have been a mingling of both, of gall and of myrrh. *And when he had tasted, he would not.* This Mark passes over in silence: *he would not drink.* This is what Mark says: *he took it not,* namely, that he should drink it.

VERS. 35.-- *They divided.* This John more distinctly: the garments into four parts, that the Church may be signified in the four parts of the world. The coat allotted signifies the unity of all the parts by the bond of charity, which comes about by lot, that is, by the grace of God, not by human choice.

VERS. 37.-- *The cause.* For which the Jews handed him over [0175A] to Pilate. The King through the cross did not lose, but confirmed, his empire, whether the Jews will or will not.

VERS. 38.-- *One on the right hand.* One on the right hand, by whom is signified the mortification of the flesh for the sake of heavenly glory: one on the left hand, by whom again is signified the mortification of the flesh for the sake of some cause of the world.

VERS. 39.-- *They blasphemed.* It had been foretold in the book of Wisdom [n: (Cap. II)]: *Let us condemn him to a most shameful death. For there shall be respect in his words. For if he be truly the Son of God, he will take him up and will deliver him from the hand of his adversaries* [var: Vulg. Sap 2:20 *erit enim ei respectus ex sermonibus illius*, and Sap 2:18 *Si enim est verus filius Dei, suscipiet illum, et liberabit eum de manibus contrariorum*]. Because therefore he was being crucified and was not delivered, they believed that he was not the Son of God: therefore they insult him as he hangs upon the tree, and shake their heads:

VERS. 40.-- *If thou be the Son of God.* If, yielding to those who insulted him, [0175B] he had come down from the cross, he would not have shown the power of patience.

VERS. 42.-- *And we will believe him* [var: Vulg. Mt 27:42 *et credimus ei*, the present tense]. A fraudulent promise: he does a greater thing in rising from the tomb, and you do not believe: if therefore he should come down from the cross, you would not believe. But the demons put this in; for they felt at once the power of the cross, and their own strength broken, and they do this that he may come down from the cross. But the Lord, knowing this, remains, that he may destroy the devil.

VERS. 44.-- *And the selfsame thing the robbers also.* At first both blasphemed, then, the signs being seen, one believed. So both peoples first blasphemed God: but the one, terrified by the signs, repented, and now convicts the Jews.

VERS. 45.-- *And from the sixth hour.* Note that the Lord is crucified when the sun is about to withdraw from the centre of the world, because [0175C] he dies for sins, and Adam, when he had sinned, heard the voice of the Lord after midday. And it is the order of reason that at the time at which he shut the gate of paradise against the transgressing Adam, at that time he should unlock it to the penitent robber. That Mark says the Lord was crucified at the third hour is for this reason, that he may show that the Jews, who excuse themselves, crucified him rather with their tongues than the soldiers by whose hands it was done: who at the third hour cried out that he should be crucified. For when he was crucified, it was about the sixth hour, that is, not yet fully the sixth.

VERS. 46.-- *And about the ninth hour.* When the day had declined toward evening and the sun had grown cool from its heat, he completes the passion, showing that he dies for our sins, by which we have fallen from the divine light and love into this night. In the morning the Lord rose again, [0175D] teaching that he would lead forth those raised up in soul into the light of eternal happiness. *Eli, Eli, lamma.* Whose nature he takes upon him, of the same men he bewails the misery. Wherein he shows how much they themselves ought to weep who sin. Marvel not at the lowliness of the words and at the complaints of one forsaken, since, knowing the form of a servant, thou seest the scandal of the cross.

VERS. 47.-- *And certain.* Not all, perhaps Romans, not knowing the property of the Hebrew speech. Or some Jews, reckoning Christ less than Elias, so that he should beg his help.

VERS. 49.-- *Let be, let us see.* Because they understood the voice of the Lord amiss, they waited in vain for the coming of Elias.

[0176A]VERS. 51.-- *And behold the veil of the temple.* That the ark of the testament and all the sacraments of the law, which were being covered, might appear and might pass over to the Gentiles. Josephus says that the angelic powers, once the guardians of the temple, then cried out together: let us pass over from these seats. The veil which was called the outer one: because now we see in part; but when that which is perfect shall come, then the inner veil shall be rent asunder. *The earth was moved.* All the elements show forth their Lord crucified. The earth is moved, not enduring to bear its Lord as he hangs. *The rocks.* That is, the hearts of the Gentiles, or the prophecies of the prophets, who are called rocks from the rock Christ, that whatever in them was shut up under the hard veil of the law might, being rent, lie open to the Gentiles.

VERS. 52.-- *And the monuments.* And yet, although the monuments [0176B] were opened, they did not rise before the Lord rose again, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren. *The bodies of the saints.* These are to be believed to have ascended in like manner with the body when the Lord ascended.

VERS. 53.-- *Into the holy city.* Jerusalem, which is called holy because of the temple, and the Holy of holies, which no other city has.

VERS. 54.-- *And the centurion.* These men confess God in the scandal of the cross. Arius in the Church preaches a creature, whom the blind Jews do not believe even for so many miracles. In the centurion is signified the faith of the Church, which, the veil of the heavenly mysteries being unlocked by the death of the Lord, affirms Jesus to be the Son of God while the Synagogue is silent.



## CHAPTER XXVII. (cont.)

VERS. 55.-- *Many women.* Matthew and Luke say that Mary Magdalen stood afar off. But John [0176C] says she was beside the cross, because she was distant by such an interval that she could be said to be beside it: because she was at hand in his sight, and afar off by comparison with the nearer crowd. We can also say that those women who were with the mother of the Lord, after he had commended her to the disciple, had already begun to go away, that they might draw themselves out of the density of the crowd and behold from farther off the other things that were done. *Ministering unto him.* It was of the Hebrew custom that women should minister of their own substance to their teachers: which the Lord accepted, that he might give an example to the apostles.

VERS. 56.-- *Of James.* James the son of Alphaeus is called the less, to distinguish him from that James who was called among the first apostles and chosen by the Lord.

VERS. 57.-- *A rich man.* Because none but a rich man could approach the governor, not that the evangelist commends [0176D] riches. He was called also a decurion, because he was of the order of the curia and discharged the office of the curia, by this he could have the means, by this, that he was a disciple, he was worthy of this ministry. *He was a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate.* Although in secret, avoiding beforehand the enmities of the Jews, in this last office he cares nothing for them.

VERS. 59.-- *In a clean linen cloth.* Mystically. He wraps Jesus in a clean linen cloth who receives him with a pure mind. Hence also the custom of the Church holds that the sacrifice of the altar be celebrated not upon silk, not upon dyed cloth, but upon pure linen.

VERS. 60.-- *In his own new monument.* Because, if he were laid in a monument where another had been laid, another [0177A] perhaps would be feigned to have risen again. In the rock, lest, if it had been built of many stones, he should be said to have been taken away by theft, the foundations of the tomb being undermined.

VERS. 61.-- *And there were there.* While the other acquaintances of Jesus were returning to their own, the women alone, who loved more closely, were watching the service of the burial, awaiting what Jesus had promised: and therefore they are the first to see the resurrection.

VERS. 63.-- *After three.* The whole from a part, of the sixth day, on which he was crucified, with its own night, for one day. The sabbath entire. The third day from its first part, that is, from the night, for the whole with its own daytime, and so there is a space of three days.

VERS. 66.-- *They made the sepulchre sure.* Their diligence profited our faith. For the more it was guarded, the more is the power of the resurrection shown.

## CHAPTER XXVIII.

[0177B]

VERS. 1.-- *In the evening,* etc. [n: (HIER.)] That the different times of these women, etc., *as far as* they could not approach, they approach in the morning. *Mary Magdalen, and the other Mary.* Two women of one name and of one devotion signify two peoples embracing with equal devotion the passion and the resurrection of Christ.

VERS. 2.-- *An earthquake.* As in the passion, so also in the resurrection there is a movement of the earth: and it signifies that the hearts of earthly men are to be moved to penance through faith in the passion and the resurrection. *He rolled back the stone.* He could go out from the sepulchre while it was closed, who was born from the virgin's womb while it was closed. The rolling back of the stone signifies the unlocking of the sacraments of Christ, which were covered by the veil of the letter: [0177C] which being taken away, the resurrection, the abolition of death, life eternal began to be preached throughout the whole world.

VERS. 3.-- *As lightning.* In the whiteness of the garment he signified that he would be gentle to the just, in the terror of the lightning he signifies that he will be terrible to the reprobate.

VERS. 5.-- *Fear not.* You who see your own fellow citizens. Let those fear who do not belong to their fellowship.

VERS. 7.-- *And going quickly.* Nor is it granted to us to keep this joy in the secret of the heart, but to lay it open to those who love in like manner.

VERS. 8.-- *With fear and joy.* The affection in them is twofold, of fear and of joy. The one from the greatness of the miracle, the other from desire of him who was rising again, and each urged on the womanly step.

[0177D]VERS. 9.-- *And behold Jesus,* etc. So Christ meets with his help all who begin the way of the virtues. *And they held.* It was said above that he went out while the monument was closed, that thou mightest understand the body to be immortal: here his feet are held, that thou mightest prove the flesh to be true. And because they trembled at so great a vision, fear is first driven out: *Fear not,* that with a peaceful mind they might be able to hear the things that are said. These women hold his feet, who adore him raised up again: but she who did not yet know that the Son of God [0178A] had risen again deservedly hears: *Touch me not, for I am not yet ascended to my Father [n: (Joan XX)]*.

VERS. 10.-- *Tell.* As a woman told the death-bearing words of the serpent, so now the words of the life-giver, that from her from whom death then came, now life may come. *To my brethren.* Before he called them servants also, now brethren, that he may teach that after the resurrection he has taken up again the same humanity, and that they may hope for the same.

VERS. 12.-- *A great sum of money. [n: (HIER.)]* Those who misuse the goods of the Church upon other things by which they may fulfil their own will are like to the scribes and the Pharisees and the priests who bought a lie and the blood of the Saviour.

VERS. 13.-- *They stole him away while we were asleep. [n: (AUG.)]* If they slept, how did they see? If they did not [0178B] see, how could they be witnesses? The avarice which took captive the disciple, the companion of the Lord, deceived also the soldiers who guarded the sepulchre: and so it seduced the Jews, whence he adds: *And it was spread abroad.*

VERS. 16.-- *They went away.* From Jerusalem into Galilee. *Into a mountain:* because the body taken up from the common earth had been lifted above all earthly things. And he admonishes us that, if we wish to see him, we should be lifted from the lowest things to the things above. Christ went before, the firstfruits of them that sleep, the others follow in their own order, and seeing him they adore him, that is, they praise him without end.

VERS. 17.-- *But some doubted,* as Luke says: thinking that they saw a spirit, which he gave up in dying.

VERS. 18.-- *And coming near.* And therefore the loving master both [0178C] strengthens them in the faith, and calls the doubting to faith, intimating to how great a glory he had come. *It is given.* He says this not of the coeternal Godhead of the Father, but of the humanity he assumed, in which he is less than the angels, in which also he was crowned with glory and honour and set above all things.

VERS. 19.-- *Going.* He who has now come into the light, which until now had for certain causes been doubtful to men. *Teach.* A fitting order. For first the hearer is to be taught. Then he is to be steeped in the sacraments of the faith, then to be instructed in the keeping of the commandments. Because unless the soul first receive the faith, baptism is not to be given, nor is it of avail to be cleansed, if afterwards he does not press on in good works.

VERS. 20.-- *And behold I am with you.* But what is the reward [0178D] of a holy manner of life, and what the pledge of the blessedness to come which the faithful have even in the present, he adds: *Behold I am with you,* etc. Which he promises to the apostles, and through their successions to the universal Church. Note that until the end of the world there will not cease to be men who are worthy of the divine dwelling.

[n: (AUG.)] On the first day of the week at daybreak, etc., *as far as* the angel saying to them: *So shall he come as you have seen him going into heaven [n: (Act. I)]*.
